entry.title: Additive cocontinuous module functors and their category
entry.statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be unital rings. A functor $F:A\text{-Mod}\to B\text{-Mod}$ is **additive cocontinuous** when it is additive and preserves every small (set-indexed) colimit. Equivalently, an additive functor is cocontinuous exactly when it preserves arbitrary direct sums and cokernels (the characterization proved in the following lemma). Restricting the functors between $A\text{-Mod}$ and $B\text{-Mod}$ to the additive cocontinuous ones, with all natural transformations as morphisms, componentwise identities and vertical composition, gives a locally small category $\mathrm{Fun}^{\mathrm{coc}}_{\mathrm{add}}(A\text{-Mod},B\text{-Mod})$. The term is a property of a functor; no commutativity of $A$ or $B$ is assumed, and no choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
Define the property on functors between the fixed module categories $A\text{-Mod}$ and $B\text{-Mod}$ ([[def-left-and-right-modules]]; both are abelian and cocomplete by [[thm-modules-over-a-ring-form-an-abelian-category]] and [[thm-rmod-is-complete-and-cocomplete]]). Cocontinuity is preservation of every small colimit in the sense of [[def-preservation-reflection-creation-continuity-and-cocontinuity]] and additivity is [[def-additive-functor]]. The class is large, so form it inside the definable-class convention of [[rem-category-theory-class-and-size-conventions]] rather than as a small functor category; [[def-functor-category]] is the small-source construction being restricted. The assertion that the restricted class is a locally small category is not free: it is justified by [[lem-additive-cocontinuous-module-functors-form-a-category]], which proves closure under identities and composition and the local-smallness argument that natural transformations are determined by their component at $A$. The right-exactness reformulation cited in the definition is proved in [[lem-additive-module-functor-preserves-colimits-iff-right-exact-and-coproduct-preserving]]; the definition itself asserts no further theorem.

**Proof technique:** construction.

references.title: M. Kamensky, Non-Commutative Algebra (BGU course notes, Spring 2017), §5.1, Theorem 5.1.43, Proposition 5.1.40, Lemma 5.1.46, Corollaries 5.1.48-5.1.49
A. Nyman and S. P. Smith, A Generalization of Watts's Theorem: Right Exact Functors on Module Categories, arXiv:0806.0832, Theorem 1.1-1.2, Propositions 3.2-3.3, Lemma 3.4

entry.title: The functor $M\otimes_A-$ is additive, right exact, and preserves direct sums over an arbitrary unital ring
entry.statement: Let $A$ be a unital ring and $M$ a right $A$-module. Then the functor $T_M=M\otimes_A-:A\text{-Mod}\to\mathbf{Ab}$ is additive, preserves cokernels (so it is right exact: every exact sequence $X\to Y\to Z\to 0$ of left $A$-modules induces an exact sequence $M\otimes_AX\to M\otimes_AY\to M\otimes_AZ\to 0$), and preserves arbitrary direct sums: the natural map $\bigoplus_{i\in I}(M\otimes_AX_i)\to M\otimes_A(\bigoplus_{i\in I}X_i)$ induced by the coordinate inclusions is an isomorphism, including $I=\varnothing$. If $M$ is a $(B,A)$-bimodule then $T_M$ takes values in left $B$-modules and all the displayed maps are $B$-linear. No commutativity of $A$ or $B$ is assumed and no choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
(1) Additivity: for parallel left $A$-linear maps $f,g:X\to Y$, both $(f+g)\otimes1$ and $f\otimes1+g\otimes1$ are group homomorphisms ([[thm-universal-property-of-module-tensor-products]], [[prop-functoriality-of-module-tensor-products]]) that agree on every elementary tensor, and elementary tensors generate ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]).

(2) Direct sums: let $\Phi=\bigoplus_i(M\otimes_AX_i)\to M\otimes_A(\bigoplus_iX_i)$ be induced by the maps $\jmath_i\otimes1$ from the universal property of the direct sum ([[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]], [[thm-universal-property-of-module-direct-sums]]), and let $\Psi$ be induced from the balanced pairing $(m,(x_i))\mapsto(m\otimes x_i)_i$, which has finite support. Then $\Psi\Phi$ fixes every $\jmath_i(m\otimes x_i)$ and $\Phi\Psi$ fixes every elementary tensor, so both composites are the identity by the two universal properties.

(3) Right exactness: given an exact $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ\to0$, the map $1\otimes g$ is surjective because $g$ is surjective and every tensor is a finite sum of elementary tensors; functoriality gives $(1\otimes g)(1\otimes f)=0$. Let $Q=(M\otimes_AY)/\operatorname{im}(1\otimes f)$ as an abelian group ([[def-quotient-group]]). For $z\in Z$ choose $y\in Y$ with $g(y)=z$ and set $b(m,z)=[m\otimes y]\in Q$; if $y'$ is another lift then $y-y'=f(x)$, so $m\otimes y-m\otimes y'=(1\otimes f)(m\otimes x)\in\operatorname{im}(1\otimes f)$ and $b$ is well defined. The identities $[(m+m')\otimes y]=[m\otimes y]+[m'\otimes y]$, $[m\otimes(y+y')]=[m\otimes y]+[m\otimes y']$ and $[(ma)\otimes y]=[m\otimes(ay)]$ make $b$ balanced, so the universal property gives $h:M\otimes_AZ\to Q$ with $h(m\otimes z)=[m\otimes y]$. Then $h\circ(1\otimes g)$ and $(1\otimes g)\circ h$ are the identity on generators, so $1\otimes g$ presents $M\otimes_AZ$ as $(M\otimes_AY)/\operatorname{im}(1\otimes f)$; hence $\ker(1\otimes g)=\operatorname{im}(1\otimes f)$ ([[def-exact-and-short-exact-sequences-of-modules]], [[def-module-homomorphism-kernel-image-and-cokernel]]).

(4) Bimodules: if $M$ is a $(B,A)$-bimodule, $M\otimes_AX$ carries the left $B$-action $b'(m\otimes x)=(b'm)\otimes x$ ([[thm-bimodule-actions-induced-on-tensor-products]]), every pairing above is $B$-linear in $m$, and every induced map is therefore $B$-linear. No step chooses elements globally, so no choice is used.

**Proof technique:** direct.

references.title: M. Kamensky, Non-Commutative Algebra (BGU course notes, Spring 2017), §5.1, Theorem 5.1.43, Proposition 5.1.40, Lemma 5.1.46, Corollaries 5.1.48-5.1.49
A. Nyman and S. P. Smith, A Generalization of Watts's Theorem: Right Exact Functors on Module Categories, arXiv:0806.0832, Theorem 1.1-1.2, Propositions 3.2-3.3, Lemma 3.4

entry.title: $F(A)$ is a $(B,A)$-bimodule for every additive functor $F$
entry.statement: Let $A,B$ be unital rings and $F:A\text{-Mod}\to B\text{-Mod}$ additive. On the left $B$-module $M=F(A)$ define, for $a\in A$ and $m\in M$, $ma:=F(r_a)(m)$, where $r_a:A\to A$, $r_a(x)=xa$ is right multiplication (a left $A$-linear endomorphism of $A$). Together with the given left $B$-action, this makes $M$ a $(B,A)$-bimodule: the right $A$-action satisfies the unit, associativity, and distributivity laws and commutes with the left $B$-action. No commutativity of the rings is assumed and no choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
Each $r_a$ is a left $A$-module endomorphism of $A$, so $F(r_a)$ is a well-defined $B$-linear endomorphism of $M$. The right-module laws follow from functoriality and additivity of $F$ ([[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]], [[def-additive-functor]]): $r_1=\mathrm{id}_A$ gives $m1=m$; $r_{a+a'}=r_a+r_{a'}$ gives $m(a+a')=ma+ma'$; $r_{aa'}=r_{a'}\circ r_a$ gives $m(aa')=(ma)a'$. The two actions commute because each $F(r_a)$ is $B$-linear: $b(ma)=bF(r_a)(m)=F(r_a)(bm)=(bm)a$. Hence $M$ is a $(B,A)$-bimodule in the sense of [[def-bimodule]]. No element of an auxiliary set is chosen.

**Proof technique:** direct.

references.title: M. Kamensky, Non-Commutative Algebra (BGU course notes, Spring 2017), §5.1, Theorem 5.1.43, Proposition 5.1.40, Lemma 5.1.46, Corollaries 5.1.48-5.1.49
A. Nyman and S. P. Smith, A Generalization of Watts's Theorem: Right Exact Functors on Module Categories, arXiv:0806.0832, Theorem 1.1-1.2, Propositions 3.2-3.3, Lemma 3.4

entry.title: Tensor-Hom adjunction for bimodules over arbitrary unital rings
entry.statement: Let $A,B$ be unital rings, $M$ a $(B,A)$-bimodule, $X$ a left $A$-module and $Y$ a left $B$-module. Then $\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,Y)$ is a left $A$-module under $(a\varphi)(m)=\varphi(ma)$, and currying $\Theta:\operatorname{Hom}_B(M\otimes_AX,Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}_A(X,\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,Y))$, $\Theta(F)(x)=[m\mapsto F(m\otimes x)]$, is a natural bijection; its inverse sends $\varphi$ to the $B$-linear map $M\otimes_AX\to Y$ determined by $m\otimes x\mapsto\varphi(x)(m)$. Consequently $T_M=M\otimes_A-$ is left adjoint to $\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,-)$. No commutativity is assumed and no choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
Well-definedness of the left $A$-action: for fixed $\varphi$ the map $m\mapsto\varphi(ma)$ is additive and $B$-linear, since $\varphi(b(ma))=(\varphi(bm))a$ by $B$-linearity of $\varphi$ and the commuting actions of [[def-bimodule]]; the module laws follow from those of $M$ and of the abelian group $\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,Y)$ ([[def-hom-groups-and-induced-hom-maps]]).

For $F\in\operatorname{Hom}_B(M\otimes_AX,Y)$, $\Theta(F)(x)$ is $B$-linear, and $\Theta(F)$ is $A$-linear because $\Theta(F)(ax)(m)=F(m\otimes ax)=F((ma)\otimes x)=\Theta(F)(x)(ma)=(a\Theta(F)(x))(m)$ by balance. For $\varphi\in\operatorname{Hom}_A(X,\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,Y))$, the prescription $u(m\otimes x)=\varphi(x)(m)$ is additive in each variable and balanced: $u(ma\otimes x)=\varphi(x)(ma)=(a\varphi(x))(m)=\varphi(ax)(m)=u(m\otimes ax)$; it is $B$-linear since each $\varphi(x)$ is. The universal property of the tensor product ([[thm-universal-property-of-module-tensor-products]]) makes $u$ well defined, and the tensor product carries the left $B$-action needed for the statement ([[thm-bimodule-actions-induced-on-tensor-products]]). The two constructions are inverse on generators, hence inverse by the universal property; naturality in $X$ and $Y$ is the commutativity of the evident squares, checked on $m\otimes x$ and using functoriality ([[prop-functoriality-of-module-tensor-products]]). This is the objectwise form of $T_M\dashv\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,-)$. No element is chosen.

**Proof technique:** direct.

references.title: M. Kamensky, Non-Commutative Algebra (BGU course notes, Spring 2017), §5.1, Theorem 5.1.43, Proposition 5.1.40, Lemma 5.1.46, Corollaries 5.1.48-5.1.49
A. Nyman and S. P. Smith, A Generalization of Watts's Theorem: Right Exact Functors on Module Categories, arXiv:0806.0832, Theorem 1.1-1.2, Propositions 3.2-3.3, Lemma 3.4

entry.title: Additive cocontinuous module functors form a locally small category
entry.statement: Let $A,B$ be unital rings. The additive cocontinuous functors $A\text{-Mod}\to B\text{-Mod}$, with all natural transformations as morphisms, componentwise identities and vertical composition, form a category. It is locally small: for any two such functors $F,G$ the map $\eta\mapsto\eta_A$ from the class of natural transformations $F\Rightarrow G$ into the set $\operatorname{Hom}_B(F(A),G(A))$ is injective, so each Hom-collection is a set. No choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
Closure and category axioms: the identity functor preserves every colimit, and a composite of additive cocontinuous functors is additive and cocontinuous because a colimit preserved by the first functor is carried to one preserved by the second; identities and vertical composition obey the functor-category laws componentwise ([[def-natural-transformation]], [[def-vertical-composition-of-natural-transformations]]).

Local smallness: fix $F,G$ and a natural $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$. For a free module $A^{(I)}=\bigoplus_{i\in I}A$ ([[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]]) naturality of $\eta$ at the coproduct inclusions $\iota_i:A\to A^{(I)}$ gives $\eta_{A^{(I)}}\circ F(\iota_i)=G(\iota_i)\circ\eta_A$; since $F$ and $G$ preserve the coproduct and the inclusions are jointly epic ([[thm-universal-property-of-module-direct-sums]]), $\eta_{A^{(I)}}$ is determined by $\eta_A$. For arbitrary $X$ take the canonical free cover $q_X:A^{(|X|)}\to X$ ([[cor-every-module-is-a-quotient-of-a-free-module]]). A cocontinuous functor is right exact, hence preserves epimorphisms ([[thm-a-left-exact-functor-preserves-monomorphisms-and-a-right-exact-functor-preserves-epimorphisms]]), so $F(q_X)$ and $G(q_X)$ are epic, and naturality $\eta_X\circ F(q_X)=G(q_X)\circ\eta_{A^{(|X|)}}$ together with the previous step determines $\eta_X$ from $\eta_A$. Therefore $\eta\mapsto\eta_A$ is injective into the set $\operatorname{Hom}_B(F(A),G(A))$, and the restricted class is a locally small category. No presentation or element is chosen globally.

**Proof technique:** direct.

references.title: M. Kamensky, Non-Commutative Algebra (BGU course notes, Spring 2017), §5.1, Theorem 5.1.43, Proposition 5.1.40, Lemma 5.1.46, Corollaries 5.1.48-5.1.49
A. Nyman and S. P. Smith, A Generalization of Watts's Theorem: Right Exact Functors on Module Categories, arXiv:0806.0832, Theorem 1.1-1.2, Propositions 3.2-3.3, Lemma 3.4

entry.title: Cocontinuity of an additive module functor equals right exactness plus coproduct preservation
entry.statement: Let $A,B$ be unital rings and $F:A\text{-Mod}\to B\text{-Mod}$ additive. Then $F$ preserves all small colimits if and only if $F$ preserves cokernels and arbitrary direct sums. Equivalently, $F$ is additive cocontinuous if and only if it is right exact (preserves every finite colimit that exists) and preserves arbitrary coproducts. No commutativity and no choice are used.
entry.proof_strategy:
($\Leftarrow$) Assume $F$ preserves cokernels and arbitrary direct sums. Let $D:\mathcal J\to A\text{-Mod}$ be a small diagram with colimit $L$. By [[thm-small-colimits-from-coproducts-and-coequalizers]] the colimit $L$ is the coequalizer of $d,c:R\rightrightarrows S$ with $R=\coprod_{u}D(j)$, $S=\coprod_jD(j)$; these colimits exist by [[thm-rmod-is-complete-and-cocomplete]]. In the additive category $A\text{-Mod}$ the coequalizer of $d,c$ is the cokernel of $d-c$ ([[cor-in-a-preadditive-category-the-coequalizer-of-a-parallel-pair-is-the-cokernel-of-their-difference]]), which $F$ preserves; and $F$ preserves the two coproducts, so $F(L)$ is the coequalizer of $F(d),F(c)$. Applying the construction theorem to $F\circ D$ identifies that coequalizer as a colimit of $F\circ D$; hence $F$ preserves all small colimits.

($\Rightarrow$) Each coproduct and each cokernel is a small colimit, so a cocontinuous $F$ preserves them; preservation of finite colimits is right exactness in the sense of [[def-left-exact-and-right-exact-functor]].

The equivalence of 'preserves cokernels' with 'right exact' for additive functors uses that an additive functor preserves finite biproducts ([[thm-an-additive-functor-preserves-finite-biproducts]]), the identification of coequalizers with cokernels of differences quoted above, and the existence of the relevant colimits in the abelian module category ([[thm-modules-over-a-ring-form-an-abelian-category]]). No step selects elements or presentations.

**Proof technique:** direct.

references.title: M. Kamensky, Non-Commutative Algebra (BGU course notes, Spring 2017), §5.1, Theorem 5.1.43, Proposition 5.1.40, Lemma 5.1.46, Corollaries 5.1.48-5.1.49
A. Nyman and S. P. Smith, A Generalization of Watts's Theorem: Right Exact Functors on Module Categories, arXiv:0806.0832, Theorem 1.1-1.2, Propositions 3.2-3.3, Lemma 3.4

entry.title: The canonical comparison to the tensor functor of $F(A)$ is balanced and natural
entry.statement: Let $A,B$ be unital rings, $F:A\text{-Mod}\to B\text{-Mod}$ additive, and $M=F(A)$ with the $(B,A)$-bimodule structure of the evaluation lemma. For $x\in X$ let $\ell_x:A\to X$, $\ell_x(a)=ax$. Then $\beta_X:M\times X\to F(X)$, $\beta_X(m,x)=F(\ell_x)(m)$, is balanced and $B$-linear in $m$, so it induces a unique group homomorphism $\tau_X:M\otimes_AX\to F(X)$ with $\tau_X(m\otimes x)=F(\ell_x)(m)$; each $\tau_X$ is $B$-linear, and $\tau:\,M\otimes_A-\Rightarrow F$ is natural: $F(u)\tau_X=\tau_Y(1_M\otimes u)$ for every left $A$-linear $u:X\to Y$. The construction of $\tau$ chooses no presentation of $X$ and no elements.
entry.proof_strategy:
Each $\ell_x$ is left $A$-linear, and $\ell_{x+x'}=\ell_x+\ell_{x'}$; additivity of $F$ gives additivity of $\beta_X$ in $x$, while $F(\ell_x)$ is additive in $m$. Balance: $\ell_{ax}=\ell_x\circ r_a$, so $\beta_X(ma,x)=F(\ell_x)F(r_a)(m)=F(\ell_{ax})(m)=\beta_X(m,ax)$. $B$-linearity in $m$: $F(\ell_x)$ is $B$-linear, and $M\otimes_AX$ carries the left $B$-action $b(m\otimes x)=(bm)\otimes x$ ([[thm-bimodule-actions-induced-on-tensor-products]]). The universal property of the tensor product ([[thm-universal-property-of-module-tensor-products]]) yields the unique homomorphism $\tau_X$ with the displayed formula, and it is $B$-linear because $\beta_X$ is $B$-linear in its first variable. Naturality: $u\circ\ell_x=\ell_{u(x)}$, hence $F(u)F(\ell_x)=F(\ell_{u(x)})$; evaluating on $m$ gives $F(u)\tau_X(m\otimes x)=\tau_Y(m\otimes u(x))=\tau_Y(1_M\otimes u)(m\otimes x)$, and elementary tensors generate ([[prop-functoriality-of-module-tensor-products]], [[def-natural-transformation]]). No presentation is chosen, so well-definedness precedes any universality or presentation claim.

**Proof technique:** direct.

references.title: M. Kamensky, Non-Commutative Algebra (BGU course notes, Spring 2017), §5.1, Theorem 5.1.43, Proposition 5.1.40, Lemma 5.1.46, Corollaries 5.1.48-5.1.49
A. Nyman and S. P. Smith, A Generalization of Watts's Theorem: Right Exact Functors on Module Categories, arXiv:0806.0832, Theorem 1.1-1.2, Propositions 3.2-3.3, Lemma 3.4

entry.title: Canonical free presentations force the comparison to be an isomorphism
entry.statement: Let $A,B$ be unital rings and $F:A\text{-Mod}\to B\text{-Mod}$ additive, right exact, and coproduct-preserving; put $M=F(A)$ with the $(B,A)$-bimodule structure of the evaluation lemma. Then the canonical comparison $\tau:M\otimes_A-\Rightarrow F$ is a natural isomorphism. Consequently $F$ is naturally isomorphic to the tensor functor $T_{F(A)}$. No commutativity and no choice are used.
entry.proof_strategy:
(i) At $A$: $\tau_A(m\otimes a)=F(\ell_a)(m)=ma$, which is the tensor-unit isomorphism $\rho_M:M\otimes_AA\to M$ ([[thm-unit-isomorphisms-for-module-tensor-products]]).

(ii) At a free module $A^{(I)}=\bigoplus_{i\in I}A$: both $F$ and $T_M$ preserve the coproduct (hypothesis; [[lem-tensoring-with-a-right-module-is-additive-right-exact-and-preserves-direct-sums]]), and naturality of $\tau$ at the coproduct inclusions exhibits $\tau_{A^{(I)}}$ as $\bigoplus_i\tau_A$ under the canonical identifications, hence an isomorphism.

(iii) At arbitrary $X$: build the canonical presentation $A^{(|K_X|)}\xrightarrow{d_X}A^{(|X|)}\xrightarrow{q_X}X\to0$, where $q_X(e_x)=x$ is the free cover of [[cor-every-module-is-a-quotient-of-a-free-module]] and $d_X$ is the composite of a free cover of $K_X=\ker q_X$ with the inclusion; it is exact at $A^{(|X|)}$ and at $X$, and the first map need not be monic ([[def-exact-and-short-exact-sequences-of-modules]]). Applying the right-exact functors $F$ and $T_M$ and the natural $\tau$ produces a map of right-exact sequences whose first two vertical arrows are isomorphisms by (ii). Cokernel universality-not a five-lemma shortcut-produces the induced map $\tau_X$ and shows it is an isomorphism: the inverse on cokernels is the unique map induced by the two inverse isomorphisms on the free terms. Hence $\tau_X$ is an isomorphism for every $X$, and $\tau$ was already natural, so $\tau$ is a natural isomorphism. No presentation independence argument is needed because $\tau$ was defined before any presentation was chosen.

**Proof technique:** direct.

references.title: M. Kamensky, Non-Commutative Algebra (BGU course notes, Spring 2017), §5.1, Theorem 5.1.43, Proposition 5.1.40, Lemma 5.1.46, Corollaries 5.1.48-5.1.49
A. Nyman and S. P. Smith, A Generalization of Watts's Theorem: Right Exact Functors on Module Categories, arXiv:0806.0832, Theorem 1.1-1.2, Propositions 3.2-3.3, Lemma 3.4
P. Etingof, S. Gelaki, D. Nikshych, V. Ostrik, Tensor Categories, §1.8, Proposition 1.8.10 (finite-dimensional free-presentation argument)

entry.title: Natural transformations between tensor functors are bimodule maps
entry.statement: Let $A,B$ be unital rings and $M,M'$ $(B,A)$-bimodules, with tensor functors $T_M=M\otimes_A-$ and $T_{M'}=M'\otimes_A-$. Under the tensor-unit isomorphisms $M\otimes_AA\cong M$ and $M'\otimes_AA\cong M'$, every natural transformation $\eta:T_M\Rightarrow T_{M'}$ corresponds to a $B$-linear map $f=\rho_{M'}^{-1}\circ\eta_A\circ\rho_M:M\to M'$ satisfying $f(ma)=f(m)a$ for all $a\in A$, i.e. a $(B,A)$-bimodule map, and then $\eta_X=f\otimes1_X$ for every left $A$-module $X$. Conversely every bimodule map $f:M\to M'$ yields a natural transformation with components $f\otimes1_X$. The two assignments are inverse bijections $\operatorname{Nat}(T_M,T_{M'})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{B\text{-}A}(M,M')$, compatible with addition, identities, and vertical composition. No commutativity and no choice are used.
entry.proof_strategy:
Given $\eta$, define $f$ by the displayed formula using the tensor-unit isomorphisms ([[thm-unit-isomorphisms-for-module-tensor-products]]); this is a $B$-linear map. Naturality of $\eta$ at the right multiplications $r_a:A\to A$ reads $\eta_A\circ(1_M\otimes r_a)=(1_{M'}\otimes r_a)\circ\eta_A$ and, evaluated on $m\otimes1$, gives $f(ma)=f(m)a$; so $f$ is a bimodule map ([[def-bimodule]]). Naturality at $\ell_x:A\to X$ reads $\eta_X\circ(1_M\otimes\ell_x)=(1_{M'}\otimes\ell_x)\circ\eta_A$ and, evaluated on $m\otimes1$, gives $\eta_X(m\otimes x)=f(m)\otimes x$; since elementary tensors generate, $\eta_X=f\otimes1_X$ and $\eta$ is determined by $f$ ([[prop-functoriality-of-module-tensor-products]]). Conversely, for a bimodule map $f$ the components $f\otimes1_X$ are natural in $X$ by functoriality of the tensor product. The correspondences preserve addition because $\otimes$ is additive on morphisms, fix identities, and respect vertical composition because $(f\otimes1_X)\circ(g\otimes1_X)=(f\circ g)\otimes1_X$; hence they are inverse bijections ([[def-hom-groups-and-induced-hom-maps]], [[def-natural-transformation]]). Nothing is chosen.

**Proof technique:** direct.

references.title: M. Kamensky, Non-Commutative Algebra (BGU course notes, Spring 2017), §5.1, Theorem 5.1.43, Proposition 5.1.40, Lemma 5.1.46, Corollaries 5.1.48-5.1.49
A. Nyman and S. P. Smith, A Generalization of Watts's Theorem: Right Exact Functors on Module Categories, arXiv:0806.0832, Theorem 1.1-1.2, Propositions 3.2-3.3, Lemma 3.4

entry.title: Eilenberg-Watts theorem for arbitrary unital rings
entry.statement: Let $A,B$ be unital rings. (i) For every $(B,A)$-bimodule $M$ the functor $T_M=M\otimes_A-$ is additive, right exact, coproduct-preserving and therefore cocontinuous, and the assignment $M\mapsto T_M$ is functorial: a bimodule map $f:M\to M'$ gives the natural transformation with components $f\otimes1_X$. (ii) Conversely every additive cocontinuous functor $F:A\text{-Mod}\to B\text{-Mod}$ is naturally isomorphic to $T_{F(A)}$, where $F(A)$ carries the $(B,A)$-bimodule structure $ma=F(r_a)(m)$. Hence, up to natural isomorphism, the additive cocontinuous functors are exactly the tensor functors with bimodule kernels: the quasi-inverse of $M\mapsto T_M$ is $F\mapsto F({}_AA)$. No commutativity of $A$ or $B$ is assumed and no choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
For (ii), the equivalence between cocontinuity and right exactness plus coproduct preservation ([[lem-additive-module-functor-preserves-colimits-iff-right-exact-and-coproduct-preserving]]) places $F$ in the class handled by [[lem-canonical-free-presentation-controls-eilenberg-watts-comparison]], whose canonical comparison $\tau:T_{F(A)}\Rightarrow F$ is built in [[lem-canonical-eilenberg-watts-comparison-is-balanced-and-natural]] and proved to be a natural isomorphism; the bimodule structure on $F(A)$ is [[lem-evaluation-on-the-regular-module-has-a-commuting-right-action]]. For (i), additivity, right exactness, and direct-sum preservation of $T_M$ are [[lem-tensoring-with-a-right-module-is-additive-right-exact-and-preserves-direct-sums]], and those give cocontinuity again by the colimit characterization; functoriality of $M\mapsto T_M$ is functoriality of the tensor product, $f\mapsto f\otimes1$. The category statement for the functor side, including local smallness of the Hom-collections appearing in the equivalence, is [[lem-additive-cocontinuous-module-functors-form-a-category]]. Every argument uses only universal properties of tensor products, direct sums, and cokernels, so neither commutativity nor choice is used.

**Proof technique:** direct.

references.title: J. Fuchs, G. Schaumann, C. Schweigert, Eilenberg-Watts calculus for finite categories and a bimodule Radford S^4 theorem, arXiv:1612.04561v3, introduction (classical statement for unital rings)
M. Kamensky, Non-Commutative Algebra (BGU course notes, Spring 2017), §5.1, Theorem 5.1.43, Proposition 5.1.40, Lemma 5.1.46, Corollaries 5.1.48-5.1.49
A. Nyman and S. P. Smith, A Generalization of Watts's Theorem: Right Exact Functors on Module Categories, arXiv:0806.0832, Theorem 1.1-1.2, Propositions 3.2-3.3, Lemma 3.4

entry.title: Eilenberg-Watts is an equivalence of Hom categories
entry.statement: Let $A,B$ be unital rings. The assignment $M\mapsto T_M$ extends to an equivalence of categories between the category of $(B,A)$-bimodules with bimodule maps and the category of additive cocontinuous functors $A\text{-Mod}\to B\text{-Mod}$ with natural transformations. It is full and faithful with $\operatorname{Nat}(T_M,T_{M'})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{B\text{-}A}(M,M')$, naturally in $M$ and $M'$, and essentially surjective by the theorem; a quasi-inverse is $F\mapsto F({}_AA)$. In particular $T_M\cong T_{M'}$ if and only if $M\cong M'$ as $(B,A)$-bimodules. No commutativity and no choice are used.
entry.proof_strategy:
Fullness and faithfulness are the bijection [[thm-natural-transformations-of-tensor-functors-are-bimodule-maps]]; it is compatible with identities and composition because $\otimes$ acts functorially and additively on morphisms, so $M\mapsto T_M$ is a functor. Essential surjectivity is part (ii) of [[thm-eilenberg-watts-for-arbitrary-unital-rings]]. A functor that is full, faithful, and essentially surjective is an equivalence, and on objects the round trip $F\mapsto F(A)\mapsto T_{F(A)}$ is the canonical natural isomorphism $\tau$ of the free-presentation lemma. The functor side is a locally small category by [[lem-additive-cocontinuous-module-functors-form-a-category]], and the bimodule side is locally small because each $\operatorname{Hom}_{B\text{-}A}(M,M')$ is a set of functions ([[def-bimodule]]), so the equivalence is an equivalence of categories in the definable-class convention. Nothing is chosen.

**Proof technique:** direct.

references.title: M. Kamensky, Non-Commutative Algebra (BGU course notes, Spring 2017), §5.1, Theorem 5.1.43, Proposition 5.1.40, Lemma 5.1.46, Corollaries 5.1.48-5.1.49
A. Nyman and S. P. Smith, A Generalization of Watts's Theorem: Right Exact Functors on Module Categories, arXiv:0806.0832, Theorem 1.1-1.2, Propositions 3.2-3.3, Lemma 3.4

entry.title: Additive cocontinuous module functors admit right adjoints
entry.statement: Let $A,B$ be unital rings. Every additive cocontinuous functor $F:A\text{-Mod}\to B\text{-Mod}$ admits a right adjoint $B\text{-Mod}\to A\text{-Mod}$: if $M$ is a $(B,A)$-bimodule with $F\cong T_M$, then $F$ is left adjoint to $\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,-)$. In particular $F$ is a left adjoint, so it preserves every colimit that exists. No commutativity and no choice are used.
entry.proof_strategy:
By [[thm-eilenberg-watts-for-arbitrary-unital-rings]], $F$ is naturally isomorphic to $T_{F(A)}$. The tensor-Hom adjunction for bimodules over arbitrary unital rings ([[lem-tensor-hom-adjunction-for-bimodules]]) gives $T_M\dashv\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,-)$ for $M=F(A)$, in the sense of [[def-adjunction-by-unit-counit-and-triangle-identities]]; conjugating the unit and counit by the natural isomorphism $F\cong T_M$ transfers the adjunction to $F$. Left adjoints preserve colimits, and the statement is not made for arbitrary functors that merely admit an adjoint; additivity is a hypothesis here.

**Proof technique:** direct.

A. Nyman and S. P. Smith, A Generalization of Watts's Theorem: Right Exact Functors on Module Categories, arXiv:0806.0832, Theorem 1.1-1.2, Propositions 3.2-3.3, Lemma 3.4

entry.title: Exact module tensor functors correspond to right-flat bimodules
entry.statement: Let $A,B$ be unital rings and $M$ a $(B,A)$-bimodule. Then the tensor functor $T_M=M\otimes_A-:A\text{-Mod}\to B\text{-Mod}$ is exact if and only if $M$ is flat as a right $A$-module. Under the Eilenberg-Watts equivalence this is a bijection between isomorphism classes of exact tensor functors $A\text{-Mod}\to B\text{-Mod}$ and right-flat $(B,A)$-bimodules. No commutativity and no choice are used.
entry.proof_strategy:
By definition ([[def-left-and-right-flat-modules-over-an-arbitrary-ring]]) the right $A$-module $M$ is flat exactly when $M\otimes_A-$ is exact on left $A$-modules, i.e. exactly when the underlying abelian-group-valued functor preserves kernels and cokernels. Kernels and cokernels in $B\text{-Mod}$ are those of the underlying abelian groups ([[def-module-homomorphism-kernel-image-and-cokernel]], [[thm-modules-over-a-ring-form-an-abelian-category]], [[thm-abelian-groups-form-an-abelian-category]]), so $T_M$ is exact as a functor of abelian categories ([[def-exact-functor-between-abelian-categories]]) if and only if its underlying functor to $\mathbf{Ab}$ is exact, which is precisely right flatness of $M$. The restriction statement follows from the Eilenberg-Watts equivalence ([[thm-eilenberg-watts-for-arbitrary-unital-rings]]): essential surjectivity identifies the exact cocontinuous functors with the tensor functors, and exactness is invariant under natural isomorphism. No left-side projectivity is asserted; projectivity of $M$ as a left $B$-module controls images of projectives, not this exactness condition. No choice is used.

**Proof technique:** direct.

A. Nyman and S. P. Smith, A Generalization of Watts's Theorem: Right Exact Functors on Module Categories, arXiv:0806.0832, Theorem 1.1-1.2, Propositions 3.2-3.3, Lemma 3.4

entry.title: Natural transformations between tensor composites are governed by bimodule maps
entry.statement: Let $A,B,C$ be unital rings, $M$ a $(B,A)$-bimodule and $N$ a $(C,B)$-bimodule, with further bimodules $M',N'$ of the same types. The associativity isomorphism $(N\otimes_BM)\otimes_AX\to N\otimes_B(M\otimes_AX)$ identifies the composite $T_N\circ T_M$ with the tensor functor $T_{N\otimes_BM}$ of the $(C,A)$-bimodule $N\otimes_BM$. Consequently natural transformations $T_N\circ T_M\Rightarrow T_{N'}\circ T_{M'}$ correspond bijectively to $(C,A)$-bimodule maps $N\otimes_BM\to N'\otimes_BM'$; each pair of bimodule maps $g:N\to N'$, $f:M\to M'$ yields the transformation with components $(g\otimes f)\otimes1_X$, $n\otimes m\otimes x\mapsto g(n)\otimes f(m)\otimes x$. Not every bimodule map $N\otimes_BM\to N'\otimes_BM'$ is of the form $g\otimes f$, and the classification covers all of them. No commutativity and no choice are used.
entry.proof_strategy:
Associativity of balanced tensor products ([[thm-associativity-of-balanced-tensor-products]]) gives the natural isomorphism $N\otimes_B(M\otimes_AX)\cong(N\otimes_BM)\otimes_AX$, and the outer actions make $N\otimes_BM$ a $(C,A)$-bimodule ( [[thm-bimodule-actions-induced-on-tensor-products]] ). Applying [[thm-natural-transformations-of-tensor-functors-are-bimodule-maps]] to the two tensor functors with kernels $N\otimes_BM$ and $N'\otimes_BM'$ gives the bijection with all $(C,A)$-bimodule maps. For a pair $(g,f)$ the formula on generators is checked using $(g\otimes f)(n\otimes m)=g(n)\otimes f(m)$; naturality and balance follow from functoriality of $\otimes$. For the final claim, over a field $k$ take $N=M=k^2$ and $N'=M'=k$; then $k^2\otimes_kk^2\cong\operatorname{Mat}_2(k)$ and a decomposition of a functional as $g\otimes f$ corresponds to a rank-one matrix, whereas the trace $\operatorname{Mat}_2(k)\to k$ is a bimodule map with matrix $I_2$ of rank two and is therefore not of the form $g\otimes f$. No step chooses a basis of an infinite-dimensional space or a presentation.

**Proof technique:** direct.

A. Nyman and S. P. Smith, A Generalization of Watts's Theorem: Right Exact Functors on Module Categories, arXiv:0806.0832, Theorem 1.1-1.2, Propositions 3.2-3.3, Lemma 3.4

entry.title: Eilenberg-Watts recovers extension of scalars
entry.statement: Let $f:R\to S$ be a unital homomorphism of commutative rings and let ${}_SS_R$ be the $(S,R)$-bimodule with left action by multiplication and right action $s\cdot r=s f(r)$ of [[def-restriction-and-extension-of-scalars]]. Then the tensor functor $T_S=S\otimes_R-$ is exactly the extension of scalars along $f$; it is additive and cocontinuous; and its Eilenberg-Watts kernel is $T_S(R)=S\otimes_RR\cong S$ with the right action of the evaluation lemma equal to the displayed action $s\cdot r=sf(r)$. Thus the Eilenberg-Watts theorem recovers extension of scalars with kernel ${}_SS_R$. The same bimodule and computation apply to an arbitrary unital ring homomorphism, but the published definition of extension of scalars is stated for commutative rings. No choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
Extension of scalars along $f$ is by definition the functor $S\otimes_R-$ ([[def-restriction-and-extension-of-scalars]]), which is $T_S$ for the displayed $(S,R)$-bimodule; it is additive, and it is cocontinuous because it is left adjoint to restriction of scalars ([[thm-extension-of-scalars-is-left-adjoint-to-restriction]], [[cor-left-adjoints-preserve-colimits]]). The tensor-unit isomorphism ([[thm-unit-isomorphisms-for-module-tensor-products]]) gives $S\otimes_RR\cong S$ by $s\otimes r\mapsto sf(r)$. Evaluating the right action of [[lem-evaluation-on-the-regular-module-has-a-commuting-right-action]] on this identification: the right multiplication $r_r$ on $R$ acts on $S\otimes_RR$ by $s\otimes x\mapsto s\otimes(xr)$, which corresponds to $s\,f(xr)=sf(x)f(r)$, so the reconstructed right action is $s\cdot r=sf(r)$, exactly the published action. Hence the kernel of the extension functor is ${}_SS_R$ and the theorem applies with no further checks. For arbitrary unital $f$, the same associativity and unit checks give a $(S,R)$-bimodule, but the published definition covers only the commutative case; that caveat is recorded, not used.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: A right exact module functor without coproduct preservation is not tensor
entry.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and let $F(V)=\prod_{n\ge0}V$ be the countable product of copies of a $k$-vector space $V$, with coordinatewise linear maps. Then $F$ is additive and exact, hence right exact, but it does not preserve coproducts: for the family $(k)_{j\in\mathbb N}$ the canonical comparison $\bigoplus_jF(k)\to F(\bigoplus_jk)$ has image the families of vectors in $\bigoplus_jk$ whose supports are contained in one fixed finite subset of $\mathbb N$, so the family $(e_n)_{n\ge0}$ of standard basis vectors is not in the image. Consequently $F$ is not naturally isomorphic to any tensor functor $T_N=N\otimes_k-$, since tensor functors preserve coproducts. Thus the coproduct-preservation hypothesis of the Eilenberg-Watts theorem cannot be dropped even for exact functors. The Axiom of Choice is used exactly to lift a countable family of surjections coordinatewise; the argument is not choice-free.
entry.proof_strategy:
Additivity of $F$ is coordinatewise. Under AC, $F$ is exact: products of injective linear maps are injective, and a countable product of surjective linear maps is surjective because a preimage can be chosen in each nonempty fibre ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Coproduct failure: identify $F(\bigoplus_jk)=\prod_n\bigoplus_jk$ and $\bigoplus_jF(k)=\bigoplus_j\prod_nk$; an element of the latter is a finite family of scalar sequences, so the $n$-th coordinate of its image is supported in the union of the finitely many supports of that family ([[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]], [[thm-universal-property-of-module-direct-sums]]). The family $(e_n)_n$, where $e_n$ is the $n$-th standard basis vector of $\bigoplus_jk$, has infinite support and is not in the image; hence the canonical comparison is not surjective and $F$ does not preserve this coproduct. If $F\cong T_N$, then $N\cong F(k)=\prod_nk$ and the natural isomorphism would conjugate the canonical comparison of $F$ to that of $T_N$; but $T_N$ preserves coproducts by the Eilenberg-Watts theorem ([[thm-eilenberg-watts-for-arbitrary-unital-rings]]), contradiction. So no tensor functor represents $F$. The only choice made is the coordinatewise selection of lifts.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: A coproduct-preserving left exact module functor is not tensor
entry.statement: Let $F(X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(\mathbb Z/2,X):\mathbf{Ab}\to\mathbf{Ab}$. Then $F$ is an additive functor of module categories over $\mathbb Z$, it preserves arbitrary direct sums (a homomorphism from the finitely generated module $\mathbb Z/2$ into a direct sum has image in a finite subsum), and it is left exact. It is not right exact: applying it to the surjection $\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z/2$ gives the zero map $0=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(\mathbb Z/2,\mathbb Z)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(\mathbb Z/2,\mathbb Z/2)\cong\mathbb Z/2$, which is not surjective. Hence $F$ is not naturally isomorphic to any tensor functor $T_N=N\otimes_{\mathbb Z}-$, because tensor functors are right exact. Thus coproduct preservation together with left exactness does not imply that a functor is tensor. No choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
Additivity: $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(\mathbb Z/2,-)$ acts on homomorphisms by postcomposition and $\operatorname{Hom}$ is an abelian group under pointwise addition ([[def-hom-groups-and-induced-hom-maps]]); postcomposition is additive. Coproduct preservation: an element $x\in\bigoplus_iX_i$ has finite support ( [[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]] ), and a homomorphism $\varphi:\mathbb Z/2\to\bigoplus_iX_i$ has $2\varphi(1)=0$, so each coordinate of $\varphi(1)$ is annihilated by 2 and the coordinates outside a finite set vanish; hence $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb Z/2,\bigoplus_iX_i)\cong\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb Z/2,X_i)$ via the canonical map, using the direct-sum universal property ([[thm-universal-property-of-module-direct-sums]]). Left exactness is [[thm-hom-functors-are-left-exact]] (covariant Hom is left exact). Failure of right exactness: $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(\mathbb Z/2,\mathbb Z)=0$ because $\mathbb Z$ has no nonzero element of order 2, so the map induced by the surjection $\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z/2$ is $0\to\mathbb Z/2$, not surjective; thus $F$ is not right exact ([[def-left-exact-and-right-exact-functor]]). If $F\cong T_N$, then $F$ would be right exact since $T_N$ is right exact by the Eilenberg-Watts theorem ([[thm-eilenberg-watts-for-arbitrary-unital-rings]]); contradiction. Hence $F$ is not tensor, even though it preserves coproducts and is left exact. No choice is used.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: Finite vector-space copowers in a $k$-linear abelian category
entry.statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $\mathcal C$ be a $k$-linear abelian category ([[def-k-linear-category-and-k-linear-functor]], [[def-abelian-category]]), let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space ([[def-dimension]], [[def-vector-space]]) and let $Y$ be an object of $\mathcal C$. Then the functor $Z\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,\mathcal C(Y,Z))$ from $\mathcal C$ to $k$-vector spaces ([[thm-the-hom-bifunctor-of-a-preadditive-category-takes-values-in-abelian-groups]]) is representable ([[def-yoneda-embedding]]): there are an object $V\odot Y$ and a natural isomorphism $\mathcal C(V\odot Y,Z)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,\mathcal C(Y,Z))$ ([[def-natural-transformation]], [[def-natural-isomorphism]]). For every finite basis $(v_1,\dots,v_n)$ of $V$ the $n$-fold biproduct $Y^n$ ([[def-biproduct]]) represents this functor through the matrix calculus of [[thm-morphisms-between-finite-biproducts-correspond-to-matrices]]; a change of basis acts by an invertible scalar matrix, and the two representations agree up to a unique compatible isomorphism ([[thm-representing-objects-are-unique-up-to-unique-compatible-isomorphism]]), so $V\odot Y$ is determined up to a unique compatible isomorphism and is independent of the chosen basis. Equivalently, $V\odot Y$ is the tensor of $Y$ by $V$ in the enriched sense of [[def-cotensor-and-tensor]]: the formula displayed above is exactly the defining corepresentation of that tensor, the base being the symmetric monoidal category of all $k$-vector spaces; it may be restricted to finite-dimensional vector spaces when all hom-spaces of $\mathcal C$ are finite-dimensional. Given a representing object with its universal element for every pair $(V,Y)$, the assignment $(V,Y)\mapsto V\odot Y$ extends canonically to a functor on the product of the category of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces with $\mathcal C$ ([[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]], [[def-additive-category]]) whose structural morphisms are induced by the representing property; identities and composition are automatic from representability. The objectwise construction uses one finite basis and one finite biproduct. The functor assertion requires the stated family of representing data; existence of each object alone does not choose such a family.
entry.proof_strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Fix the finite basis $(v_1,\dots,v_n)$ of $V$ and let $A=Y^n$ be the supplied $n$-fold biproduct of $Y$ with injections $i_1,\dots,i_n$; for $n=0$ this is the empty biproduct, the zero object ([[def-biproduct]], [[def-additive-category]]). For each object $Z$ the evaluations $f\mapsto(f(v_1),\dots,f(v_n))$ and $g\mapsto(g\circ i_1,\dots,g\circ i_n)$ are bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,\mathcal C(Y,Z))\to\mathcal C(Y,Z)^n$ and $\mathcal C(A,Z)\to\mathcal C(Y,Z)^n$ by [F1] and [F2], so their composite is a bijection
$$\eta_Z:\mathcal C(A,Z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,\mathcal C(Y,Z)).$$
For $u:Z\to Z'$ both $\eta_{Z'}(u\circ g)$ and the componentwise composite $u\circ\eta_Z(g)$ have $j$-th entry $u\circ g\circ i_j$, so $\eta$ is natural in $Z$ ([[def-natural-transformation]], [[thm-the-hom-bifunctor-of-a-preadditive-category-takes-values-in-abelian-groups]]); the universal element $u_A=\eta_A(1_A)$ is the linear map with $u_A(v_j)=i_j$, so $(A,u_A)$ represents the functor $Z\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,\mathcal C(Y,Z))$ ([[def-yoneda-embedding]], [[def-natural-isomorphism]]). [given, F1, F2]

2.1 Let $(v'_1,\dots,v'_n)$ be a second finite basis and write $v'_k=\sum_j s_{jk}v_j$ for the invertible scalar matrix $S=(s_{jk})$ ([[def-linear-map]]). The associated representation is $(A,u'_A)$ with $u'_A(v'_k)=i_k$; by linearity and [F2] there is a unique endomorphism $\phi:A\to A$ with $\phi\circ u_A=u'_A$, its matrix being determined by $S$, and the same construction with the two bases interchanged gives a two-sided inverse, so $\phi$ is invertible. By [F4] applied to the two universal elements of the functor of step 1.1, $\phi$ is the unique compatible isomorphism between the two representing objects; hence $V\odot Y$ is determined up to a unique compatible isomorphism and is independent of the chosen basis of $V$. [step 1.1, F4, algebra]

2.2 Let $h:Y\to Y'$ and let $(A',u')$ be the representation of $Z\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,\mathcal C(Y',Z))$ produced by step 1.1, with natural bijections $\eta'_Z$. Precomposition with $h$ gives maps $h_*:\mathcal C(Y',Z)\to\mathcal C(Y,Z)$, $g\mapsto g\circ h$, componentwise linear, and the composite $\theta_Z:=(\eta_Z)^{-1}\circ h_*\circ\eta'_Z$ is a natural transformation $\mathcal C(A',-)\Rightarrow\mathcal C(A,-)$ ([[def-natural-transformation]], [[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]]). By [F3] applied to the objects $A'$ and $A$ there is a unique morphism $\phi_h:A\to A'$ with $\theta_Z(f)=f\circ\phi_h$ for every $f:A'\to Z$, and this is the structural morphism $V\odot Y\to V\odot Y'$ induced by the representing property. [step 1.1, F3, given]

2.3 Let $\lambda:V\to V'$ be a $k$-linear map. Precomposition gives $\lambda^*:\operatorname{Hom}_k(V',\mathcal C(Y,Z))\to\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,\mathcal C(Y,Z))$, $g\mapsto g\circ\lambda$, and the composite $(\eta^{V}_Z)^{-1}\circ\lambda^*\circ\eta^{V'}_Z$ is a natural transformation $\mathcal C(A^{V'},-)\Rightarrow\mathcal C(A^{V},-)$; by [F3] it is induced by a unique morphism $V\odot Y\to V'\odot Y$, the structural morphism in the coefficient variable ([[def-k-linear-category-and-k-linear-functor]], [[def-linear-map]]). [step 1.1, F3]

3.1 For natural transformations $\alpha:\mathcal C(A,-)\Rightarrow\mathcal C(B,-)$ and $\beta:\mathcal C(B,-)\Rightarrow\mathcal C(C,-)$, [F3] gives $\alpha_c(f)=f\circ E(\alpha)$ and $\beta_c(g)=g\circ E(\beta)$, hence $E(\beta\circ\alpha)=E(\alpha)\circ E(\beta)$; identities correspond to identities. Now take the family of representing objects and universal elements in the statement as supplied data. The transformations in steps 2.2 and 2.3 go opposite to the corresponding maps of pairs, and their composites act by $g\mapsto g\circ h\circ h'$ in the object variable and by $f\mapsto f\circ\lambda'\circ\lambda$ in the coefficient variable. These operations commute with one another, so their representing morphisms preserve identities and composition and give the asserted functor $(V,Y)\mapsto V\odot Y$. This proves functoriality of the supplied family, without selecting one globally from objectwise existence. [step 2.2, step 2.3, F3]


4.1 The isomorphism $\mathcal C(V\odot Y,Z)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,\mathcal C(Y,Z))$ is $k$-linear, since basis evaluation and composition with the biproduct injections are $k$-linear. It is therefore the enriched tensor isomorphism of [F5] over all $k$-vector spaces. A finite-dimensional enriching base is available only when all hom-spaces of $\mathcal C$ are finite-dimensional. The objectwise existence and basis comparison require only finite data; functoriality uses the supplied family as in step 3.1. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, F5, given] ∎

entry.title: The Deligne product of finite linear categories
entry.statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be finite $k$-linear abelian categories ([[def-finite-k-linear-abelian-category]], [[def-k-linear-category-and-k-linear-functor]], [[def-abelian-category]]). A **Deligne product** of $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ is a $k$-linear abelian category $\mathcal C\boxtimes\mathcal D$ together with a functor $\boxtimes:\mathcal C\times\mathcal D\to\mathcal C\boxtimes\mathcal D$ ([[def-product-category]]) that is $k$-linear in each variable, right exact in each variable ([[def-left-exact-and-right-exact-functor]]), and universal with these properties: for every $k$-linear abelian category $\mathcal E$ the restriction functor $G\mapsto G\circ\boxtimes$, from $k$-linear right exact functors $\mathcal C\boxtimes\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ with all natural transformations to $k$-linear functors $\mathcal C\times\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ right exact in each variable with all natural transformations ([[def-functor-category]], [[def-natural-transformation]]), is an equivalence of categories ([[def-equivalence-and-adjoint-equivalence-of-categories]]). The universal property is an equivalence of categories, not merely a bijection on functor objects; existence is not asserted here but is supplied by [[thm-finite-deligne-products-exist-by-tensor-product-algebras]], and uniqueness means an equivalence respecting the universal bifunctor. Bilinearity is expressed through the action of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces that every $k$-linear abelian category carries by the finite copowers of [[lem-finite-vector-space-copowers-in-a-linear-abelian-category]]; the class and size bookkeeping is that of [[rem-category-theory-class-and-size-conventions]], and no choice beyond the supplied finite universal-object data is made.
entry.proof_strategy:
This is a definition: it fixes the data (a $k$-linear abelian category with a $k$-bilinear bifunctor right exact in each variable) and the universal property (an equivalence of functor categories), and it asserts no existence. The only well-definedness obligations are that 'right exact in each variable' has the meaning of [[def-left-exact-and-right-exact-functor]] for the partial functors $\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$, that bilinearity is the enrichment of [[def-k-linear-category-and-k-linear-functor]] together with the finite copower action of [[lem-finite-vector-space-copowers-in-a-linear-abelian-category]], and that the functor categories are formed under the class conventions of [[rem-category-theory-class-and-size-conventions]] ([[def-functor-category]], [[def-equivalence-and-adjoint-equivalence-of-categories]]). Existence, uniqueness and the identification of the universal bifunctor are not assumed; they are proved in [[thm-finite-deligne-products-exist-by-tensor-product-algebras]] for finite categories.

**Proof technique:** define.

entry.title: Bilinear right exact functors are determined by their value on the regular modules
entry.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $R$ and $S$ be finite-dimensional unital $k$-algebras ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], [[def-dimension]]) with $R\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ and $S\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ the categories of finite-dimensional left modules ([[def-left-and-right-modules]]), let $\mathcal E$ be a $k$-linear abelian category ([[def-abelian-category]], [[def-k-linear-category-and-k-linear-functor]]), and let $H:R\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\times S\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\to\mathcal E$ be $k$-linear and right exact in each variable ([[def-product-category]], [[def-left-exact-and-right-exact-functor]]). Put $T=R\otimes_kS$ ([[thm-tensor-product-of-algebras-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and $W=H(R,S)$. Right multiplications in the two variables make $W$ a right $R$-module and a right $S$-module by endomorphisms, with commuting actions, hence a right $T$-module, and this structure is functorial in $H$. Then (i) the finite free presentations of $T\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ construct a functor $\bar H:T\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\to\mathcal E$ from that right $T$-module structure, and a canonical natural isomorphism ([[def-natural-isomorphism]]) $\bar H(X\otimes_kY)\cong H(X,Y)$, natural in $X\in R\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ and $Y\in S\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$, where $X\otimes_kY$ carries the commuting $R$- and $S$-actions; and (ii) every natural transformation ([[def-natural-transformation]]) $\eta:H\Rightarrow H'$ between two such bifunctors is determined by its component $\eta_{R,S}$, and $\eta\mapsto\eta_{R,S}$ is a bijection onto the compatible maps of right $T$-modules. The lemma asserts no existence of a Deligne product (existence is established on this page); it identifies how every such bifunctor is computed from its value on $(R,S)$, The simultaneous selection of presentations and cokernels uses the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]); morphisms and comparison isomorphisms are independent of those selections.

Module and functor categories are formed on chosen small module representatives. A right $T$-module object $W$ in $\mathcal E$ means a $k$-linear anti-homomorphism $T\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal E}(W)$; no underlying set of elements of $W$ is assumed.
entry.proof_strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Put $\rho(a)=H(r_a,1_S)$ and $\sigma(c)=H(1_R,r_c)$, where $r_a(x)=xa$ and $r_c(y)=yc$. These are $k$-linear in $a,c$, unital, and satisfy $\rho(ab)=\rho(b)\rho(a)$ and $\sigma(cc')=\sigma(c')\sigma(c)$. The two families commute by functoriality on the product category, so the bilinear map $(a,c)\mapsto\sigma(c)\rho(a)$ descends through $R\otimes_kS$ to a unital anti-homomorphism $\tau:T\to\operatorname{End}(W)$. This is the right $T$-action on $W$. Naturality shows that $\eta_{R,S}$ commutes with $\tau(t)$ for every $t$. [given, F2, F3, F7]

2.1 On finite free left $T$-modules put $K(T^n)=W^n$. A left-linear map $\varphi:T^m\to T^n$ is determined by $\varphi(e_j)=\sum_i p_{ij}e_i$, hence $\varphi(x)_i=\sum_j x_jp_{ij}$. Define $K(\varphi)$ to have $(i,j)$-entry $\tau(p_{ij})$. If $\psi$ has entries $q_{\ell i}$, then $\psi\varphi$ has entries $\sum_i p_{ij}q_{\ell i}$, and $\tau(p_{ij}q_{\ell i})=\tau(q_{\ell i})\tau(p_{ij})$, proving $K(\psi\varphi)=K(\psi)K(\varphi)$. Identities are preserved, so this is a $k$-linear functor on free modules. [step 1.1, F3, F4]

3.1 For a presentation $P=(T^m\xrightarrow{\delta}T^n\xrightarrow{\pi}Z\to0)$ put $K(P)=\operatorname{coker}K(\delta)$, with projection $q_P$. A map $u:Z\to Z'$ lifts to $g:T^n\to T^{n'}$ by lifting its finitely many generator images through $\pi'$. The map $g\delta$ lands in $\operatorname{im}\delta'$, so lifting the finitely many generator images again gives $g\delta=\delta'v$. Thus $q_{P'}K(g)K(\delta)=0$, and $K(g)$ descends to a map $K(P)\to K(P')$. Two lifts differ by $\delta'v'$ for the same reason, so their descended maps agree. Identity lifts and composites of lifts give identities and composition. [step 2.1, F1, F5]

4.1 Applying step 3.1 to the identity of $Z$ gives canonical mutually inverse comparisons between $K(P)$ and $K(P')$ for any two presentations. On the small module source, choose one presentation per object and one cokernel per resulting map, and put $\bar H(Z)=K(P_Z)$. These simultaneous choices use [[def-axiom-of-choice]], not merely the finite choice used for each lift. For a class-sized definable target, collection first bounds a set of witnesses for this set-indexed family and AC selects them. The lift-independent maps of step 3.1 define a $k$-linear functor; other choices give a canonical natural isomorphism. Fix these presentation and cokernel data for the construction. [step 3.1, F1, F5, given]

5.1 Choose presentations $R^s\xrightarrow d R^r\to X\to0$ and $S^{s'}\xrightarrow{d'}S^{r'}\to Y\to0$. Then $X\otimes_kY$ has the presentation $T^{sr'}\oplus T^{rs'}\xrightarrow{(d\otimes1,1\otimes d')}T^{rr'}\longrightarrow X\otimes_kY\longrightarrow0.$ Indeed its last term is the quotient of $R^r\otimes_kS^{r'}$ by the two images: sending $(\bar x,\bar y)$ to the class of $x\otimes y$ is well defined and bilinear, and the tensor universal property gives an inverse to the induced quotient map. The identifications $R^a\otimes_kS^b\cong T^{ab}$ preserve the left $T$-actions. [step 4.1, F1, F6, given]

6.1 Right exactness and additivity in each variable identify $H(R^a,S^b)$ with $W^{ab}$ and compute $H(X,Y)$ as the successive cokernel of the maps induced by $d'$ and $d$. Their entries are precisely the action endomorphisms in step 1.1. These successive cokernels are the cokernel of the pair of maps in step 5.1 after applying $K$: a map out of $W^{rr'}$ factors through either description exactly when it kills both maps. The universal property [F5] therefore gives $\bar H(X\otimes_kY)\cong H(X,Y)$. Lifting maps between the presentations shows that both sides use the same matrices; step 3.1 removes dependence on the lifts. The comparison is consequently natural in both variables. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, F3, F4, F5]

7.1 Naturality against biproduct injections and projections determines $\eta_{R^a,S^b}$ from $\eta_{R,S}$. Naturality against the presentation surjections, which $H,H'$ send to epimorphisms, then determines $\eta_{X,Y}$, proving injectivity. Conversely a morphism $f:W\to W'$ commuting with the right $T$-actions gives componentwise maps $W^{ab}\to W'^{ab}$ commuting with all free-pair matrices. They descend through the successive cokernels of step 6.1. Lifts as in step 3.1 show these components are independent of presentations and natural in $X,Y$, and the component at $(R,S)$ is $f$. Thus evaluation is a bijection onto compatible morphisms of right $T$-module objects. [step 1.1, step 3.1, step 6.1, F3, F4, F5, F7]

8.1 Steps 4.1 and 6.1 prove (i), and step 7.1 proves (ii). The construction uses AC for its set-indexed object data; all lift choices are finite and induce unique maps on cokernels. No commutativity of $R$ or $S$ is used. [step 4.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, given] ∎

entry.title: Finite Deligne products exist via tensor-product algebras
entry.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field and let $R,S$ be finite-dimensional unital $k$-algebras, with finite-dimensional left module categories $R\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$, $S\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], [[def-dimension]], [[def-left-and-right-modules]]). Put $T=R\otimes_kS$ ([[thm-tensor-product-of-algebras-over-a-commutative-ring]]). (i) The functor $\boxtimes:R\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\times S\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\to T\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ ([[def-product-category]]), $(X,Y)\mapsto X\otimes_kY$ with $(r\otimes s)(x\otimes y)=rx\otimes sy$ ([[thm-universal-property-of-module-tensor-products]], [[thm-bimodule-actions-induced-on-tensor-products]], [[prop-functoriality-of-module-tensor-products]]), is $k$-linear in each variable ([[def-k-linear-category-and-k-linear-functor]]) and right exact in each variable ([[def-left-exact-and-right-exact-functor]]). (ii) For every $k$-linear abelian category $\mathcal E$ ([[def-abelian-category]]), restriction along $\boxtimes$ is an equivalence of categories from $k$-linear right exact functors $T\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\to\mathcal E$ with all natural transformations to $k$-linear functors $R\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\times S\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\to\mathcal E$ right exact in each variable with all natural transformations ([[def-functor-category]], [[def-natural-transformation]], [[def-equivalence-and-adjoint-equivalence-of-categories]]); a quasi-inverse sends $H$ to the functor $\bar H$ built from $W=H(R,S)$ and its right $T$-action as in [[lem-bilinear-right-exact-functors-are-determined-by-the-pair-of-regular-modules]]. (iii) Consequently $T\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ together with $\boxtimes$ is a Deligne product of $R\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ and $S\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ in the sense of [[def-deligne-product-of-finite-linear-categories]]: it is finite $k$-linear abelian ([[def-finite-k-linear-abelian-category]], [[prop-finite-dimensional-module-categories-are-intrinsically-finite]], [[thm-dimension-formula]]), and the universal property holds. For abstract finite $k$-linear abelian categories, transporting along chosen module models ([[thm-finite-abelian-categories-are-finite-dimensional-module-categories]]) yields a Deligne product, well defined up to an equivalence respecting the universal bifunctors. No commutativity of $R$ or $S$ is assumed. AC is used for the set-indexed presentation and universal-object selections, as in the determination lemma.

All module sources and functor categories use chosen small representatives; transport along supplied module equivalences is understood.
entry.proof_strategy:
**Proof technique:** constructive.

1.1 By [F1] the tensor product $X\otimes_kY$ carries commuting left actions of $R$ and $S$, hence the left $T$-action $(r\otimes s)(x\otimes y)=rx\otimes sy$ of the $k$-algebra $T=R\otimes_kS$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]), and it is functorial in both variables with the identity and composition laws [F2]; choosing a finite basis of $X$ identifies $X\otimes_kY$ with a finite direct sum of copies of $Y$ by the universal property of [F2], so $\dim_k(X\otimes_kY)=\dim_kX\cdot\dim_kY$ [F6] and $\boxtimes$ lands in the finite-dimensional category $T\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ ([[def-dimension]]). Each partial functor is $k$-linear because additivity and scalar multiplication are read off on generators, where $(f+f')\otimes1=f\otimes1+f'\otimes1$ and $(\lambda f)\otimes1=\lambda(f\otimes1)$, and the maps are determined by their values on generators [F2]; hence $(X,Y)\mapsto X\otimes_kY$ is $k$-linear in each variable ([[def-k-linear-category-and-k-linear-functor]], [[def-product-category]]). [given, F1, F2, F6]

2.1 For fixed $Y$ the functor $X\mapsto X\otimes_kY$ preserves cokernels: if $q:X\to X'$ is the cokernel of $f:X''\to X$, so that $\ker q=\operatorname{im}f$ ([[def-exact-and-short-exact-sequences-of-modules]], [[def-module-homomorphism-kernel-image-and-cokernel]]), then $q\otimes1$ is surjective with $\operatorname{im}(f\otimes1)\subseteq\ker(q\otimes1)$, and the balanced map sending $(x',y)$ with $q(x)=x'$ to the class of $x\otimes y$ is well defined because representatives differ by an element of $\ker q=\operatorname{im}f$, and it induces a two-sided inverse of the map on generators [F2]; hence $\ker(q\otimes1)=\operatorname{im}(f\otimes1)$. The functor is additive by the same generator computation, so it preserves finite coproducts and cokernels and therefore every finite colimit, that is, it is right exact ([[def-left-exact-and-right-exact-functor]], [[thm-an-additive-functor-preserves-finite-biproducts]]); the argument in the first variable is identical, so $\boxtimes$ is right exact in each variable. [step 1.1, F2, F7]

3.1 Let $G,G':T\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\to\mathcal E$ be $k$-linear and right exact. Both $G\circ\boxtimes$ and $G'\circ\boxtimes$ are $k$-linear and right exact in each variable by step 2.1, so [F3] applies to the pair $(G\circ\boxtimes,G'\circ\boxtimes)$ and gives a bijection $\operatorname{Nat}(G\circ\boxtimes,G'\circ\boxtimes)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(G(T),G'(T))$ onto right $T$-module maps, by evaluation at $(R,S)$. Applying [F3] with the second algebra $k$ to the bifunctors $(Z,V)\mapsto G(Z\otimes_kV)$ and $(Z,V)\mapsto G'(Z\otimes_kV)$, whose value at $(T,k)$ is $G(T\otimes_kk)\cong G(T)$, gives in the same way a bijection $\operatorname{Nat}(G,G')\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(G(T),G'(T))$: injectivity because the component at $(Z,k)$ recovers $\eta_Z$ under the natural isomorphism $Z\otimes_kk\cong Z$, and surjectivity because the extension of a right $T$-module map constructed by [F3] is natural and has the prescribed component. Since $(\eta\circ\boxtimes)_{R,S}=\eta_T$, composition with $\boxtimes$ identifies these two bijections, so restriction along $\boxtimes$ is fully faithful. [step 2.1, F3]

4.1 Let $H$ be a $k$-linear bifunctor right exact in each variable and let $\bar H$ be the functor constructed from $W=H(R,S)$ in [F3]. Write $K$ for the functor on finite free $T$-modules used in that construction. Then $\bar H$ is $k$-linear: if $g_u,g_v$ are lifts of $u,v:Z\to Z'$ between the chosen presentations, then $g_u+g_v$ lifts $u+v$ and the induced map on cokernels is additive in the lift by the uniqueness in [F7], so $\bar H(u+v)=\bar H(u)+\bar H(v)$, and $g_{\lambda u}=\lambda g_u$ gives $\bar H(\lambda u)=\lambda\bar H(u)$ similarly. It is right exact: for a presentation $T^m\xrightarrow{\delta}T^n\to Z\to0$ the universal property of the cokernel [F7] gives a bijection $\mathcal E(\bar H(Z),E')\cong\{h:W^n\to E':hK(\delta)=0\}$ natural in $E'$, and the right-hand side is the set of $T$-linear maps $Z\to\mathcal E(W,E')$ under the left $T$-action $(t\cdot\varphi)(w)=\varphi(w\cdot t)$ on the hom-object, a map $h$ corresponding to the family of its components $h\,i_j:W\to E'$ and the condition $hK(\delta)=0$ saying exactly that this family annihilates $\delta(T^m)$; hence a cokernel sequence $Z''\to Z\to Z'\to0$ in $T\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ gives exact sequences $0\to\mathcal E(\bar H(Z'),E')\to\mathcal E(\bar H(Z),E')\to\mathcal E(\bar H(Z''),E')$ for all $E'$, which by the characterization in [F7] says that $\bar H(Z'')\to\bar H(Z)\to\bar H(Z')$ is again a cokernel sequence. So $\bar H$ preserves cokernels and, being additive, all finite colimits, that is, it is right exact ([[def-left-exact-and-right-exact-functor]], [[thm-an-additive-functor-preserves-finite-biproducts]], [[def-abelian-category]]). By [F3] there is a natural isomorphism $\bar H\circ\boxtimes\cong H$. Fix presentation data once on the small source. The construction on compatible action maps in the determination lemma then makes $H\mapsto\bar H$ a functor, with $\bar H\circ\boxtimes\cong H$ natural in $H$. Full faithfulness from step 3.1 lifts this comparison uniquely to $\overline{G\circ\boxtimes}\cong G$, natural in $G$, so restriction and this functor are quasi-inverse, giving an equivalence of categories ([[def-equivalence-and-adjoint-equivalence-of-categories]], [[def-functor-category]], [[def-natural-transformation]], [[rem-category-theory-class-and-size-conventions]]). [step 3.1, F3, F7, construct]

5.1 By [F4] $T\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ is an abelian $k$-linear category, and because $\dim_kT=\dim_kR\cdot\dim_kS$ is finite [F6] while the module category of a finite-dimensional $k$-algebra is intrinsically finite [F4], $T\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ is a finite $k$-linear abelian category in the sense of [[def-finite-k-linear-abelian-category]]; the equivalence of step 4.1, required for every $k$-linear abelian $\mathcal E$, is exactly the universal property of [[def-deligne-product-of-finite-linear-categories]], so $T\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ with $\boxtimes$ is a Deligne product of $R\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ and $S\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$. For abstract finite $k$-linear abelian categories $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$, [F5] provides equivalences $\mathcal A\simeq R\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$, $\mathcal B\simeq S\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ with $R,S$ finite-dimensional, and transporting $\boxtimes$, the finite direct sums, the algebra $T$ and the universal property along them yields a Deligne product of $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$, well defined up to an equivalence respecting the universal bifunctors as follows directly from the universal property: for two products $P,Q$, extend their universal bifunctors to right exact functors $P\to Q$ and $Q\to P$. The restrictions of both composites are isomorphic to the corresponding universal bifunctors, so full faithfulness of restriction lifts these isomorphisms to composites isomorphic to the identities. No commutativity of $R$ or $S$ was used. The construction inherits the set-indexed choices of [F3], made under the stated AC assumption. [step 4.1, F4, F5, F6, discharge-construct] ∎

entry.title: The opposite Deligne product is the category of finite bimodules
entry.statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be finite $k$-linear abelian categories with supplied module equivalences $\mathcal A\simeq R\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$, $\mathcal B\simeq S\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$; use chosen small representatives. Here $(\mathcal B,\mathcal A)\text{-}\mathrm{bimod}$ denotes the finite $k$-linear $(S,R)$-bimodules in these models, not modules over abstract categories themselves. Then there is an equivalence of $k$-linear categories $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\boxtimes\mathcal B\simeq(\mathcal B,\mathcal A)\text{-}\mathrm{bimod}$ between the Deligne product of [[thm-finite-deligne-products-exist-by-tensor-product-algebras]] and the category of finite-dimensional $(\mathcal B,\mathcal A)$-bimodules ([[def-bimodule]], [[def-opposite-category]]), carrying an external object $\bar a\boxtimes b$ to $b\otimes_ka^*$, where $a^*$ is the $k$-dual of $a$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]], [[def-vector-space]]) with the induced right $\mathcal A$-action and $b$ keeps its left $\mathcal B$-action ([[def-left-and-right-modules]]). The equivalence is the transport of the identification $(R^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes_kS)\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\cong(\mathcal B,\mathcal A)\text{-}\mathrm{bimod}$ ([[def-opposite-ring]], [[thm-tensor-product-of-algebras-over-a-commutative-ring]], [[thm-modules-over-a-ring-form-an-abelian-category]]) along module models ([[thm-finite-abelian-categories-are-finite-dimensional-module-categories]]) and the exact contravariant duality $(-)^*$ ([[lem-finite-module-duality-is-exact-with-commuting-bimodule-actions]]). Moreover the universal property dualises: the bifunctor $\boxtimes$ is also left exact in each variable, restriction along it induces equivalences for left-exact-in-each-variable bifunctors as well, and $(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\boxtimes\mathcal B)^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq\mathcal A\boxtimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$, so the left exact external-tensor formula of the categorical Eilenberg–Watts triangle on this page is an instance of the universal property in its dual form. The Deligne-product construction is under the AC assumption of its cited existence theorem; the duality and action identifications require no further choice.
entry.proof_strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Use the supplied finite-dimensional unital $k$-algebras $R,S$ and $k$-linear equivalences of [F1] $\mathcal A\simeq R\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$, $\mathcal B\simeq S\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ ([[def-equivalence-and-adjoint-equivalence-of-categories]], [[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], [[def-dimension]]). The $k$-dual $X^*=\operatorname{Hom}_k(X,k)$ with the right $R$-action $(\lambda\cdot a)(x)=\lambda(ax)$, equivalently the left $R^{\mathrm{op}}$-action $a\cdot\lambda:=\lambda\cdot a$, is a contravariant exact equivalence to $R^{\mathrm{op}}\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ [F2] ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]), so it identifies $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $R^{\mathrm{op}}\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ ([[def-opposite-category]], [[def-opposite-ring]]); $R^{\mathrm{op}}\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ and $S\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ are finite $k$-linear abelian categories [F6] ([[def-abelian-category]], [[def-k-linear-category-and-k-linear-functor]]). [given, F1, F2, F6]

2.1 By [F3] applied to the finite-dimensional algebras $R^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $S$, the category $(R^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes_kS)\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ with its tensor bifunctor is a Deligne product of $R^{\mathrm{op}}\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ and $S\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$, so transporting along step 1.1 identifies $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\boxtimes\mathcal B$ with $(R^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes_kS)\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$. A left module over $R^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes_kS$ is a $k$-vector space with commuting left $R^{\mathrm{op}}$- and left $S$-actions [F4], that is, a $k$-vector space with a right $R$-action and a left $S$-action that commute, i.e. a finite-dimensional $(S,R)$-bimodule ([[def-bimodule]], [[def-left-and-right-modules]], [[def-vector-space]], [[thm-modules-over-a-ring-form-an-abelian-category]]); under the equivalences of step 1.1 this is exactly the category $(\mathcal B,\mathcal A)\text{-}\mathrm{bimod}$ of finite-dimensional $(\mathcal B,\mathcal A)$-bimodules, so $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\boxtimes\mathcal B\simeq(\mathcal B,\mathcal A)\text{-}\mathrm{bimod}$ as $k$-linear categories. [step 1.1, F3, F4]

3.1 The universal bifunctor of $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\boxtimes\mathcal B$ is the transport of the tensor bifunctor of $R^{\mathrm{op}}\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\times S\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$, so on the external object $\bar a\boxtimes b$ it sends $(a,b)$ to $a^*\otimes_kb$, where $a^*=\operatorname{Hom}_k(a,k)$ carries the induced right $\mathcal A$-action and $b$ its left $\mathcal B$-action [F2, F4, F5]. The symmetry of the tensor product over the field, induced by the balanced map $(x,y)\mapsto y\otimes x$ and unique factorization through the tensor product [F5], is a natural isomorphism $a^*\otimes_kb\cong b\otimes_ka^*$ compatible with the two actions ([[prop-functoriality-of-module-tensor-products]], [[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]), so the equivalence carries $\bar a\boxtimes b$ to $b\otimes_ka^*$ with those actions, as asserted. [step 2.1, F4, F5]

3.2 The tensor product of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces is exact in each variable: if $f:Y\to Y'$ is injective, then a $k$-linear retraction $r$ of $f$ exists because a basis of the image of $f$ extends to a basis of the finite-dimensional space $Y'$ ([[def-dimension]]), and $(1\otimes r)(1\otimes f)=1$ by functoriality [F5], so $1\otimes f$ is injective; right exactness in each variable holds by [F3](i), so $\boxtimes$ is also left exact in each variable ([[def-left-exact-and-right-exact-functor]]). Passing to opposites, $((R^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes_kS)\text{-}\mathrm{mod})^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq(R\otimes_kS^{\mathrm{op}})\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$, via the finite contravariant duality of [F2] for the algebra $R^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes_kS$, followed by the algebra isomorphism $(R^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes_kS)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong R\otimes_kS^{\mathrm{op}}$, checked on elementary tensors [F4, F7]; by [F3] the category $(R\otimes_kS^{\mathrm{op}})\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ with its tensor bifunctor is a Deligne product of $R\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ and $S^{\mathrm{op}}\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$, so transporting along step 1.1 gives the canonical equivalence $(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\boxtimes\mathcal B)^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq\mathcal A\boxtimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F3, F5, F7]

4.1 The universal property dualises: a $k$-linear functor $G$ out of $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\boxtimes\mathcal B$ is left exact exactly when its opposite functor out of $(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\boxtimes\mathcal B)^{\mathrm{op}}$ is right exact [F7], and step 3.2 identifies that opposite source with $\mathcal A\boxtimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$, where [F3] is the equivalence $\operatorname{Rex}_k(\mathcal A\boxtimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}})\simeq\operatorname{Rex}_{k,k}(\mathcal A\times\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}})$ for every $k$-linear abelian $\mathcal E$; applying the same duality to the bifunctors turns right exactness in each variable on $\mathcal A\times\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$ into left exactness in each variable on $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal B$ [F7], so restriction along $\boxtimes$ induces an equivalence $\operatorname{Lex}_k(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\boxtimes\mathcal B,\mathcal E)\simeq\operatorname{Lex}_{k,k}(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal B,\mathcal E)$ as well ([[def-equivalence-and-adjoint-equivalence-of-categories]], [[def-functor-category]], [[def-natural-transformation]]); the left exact external-tensor formula of the categorical Eilenberg–Watts triangle on this page is therefore an instance of the universal property in its dual form. A second choice of module models is related to the first by a $k$-linear equivalence [F1], and conjugating by it identifies the transported equivalences together with their universal bifunctors, so the construction is well defined up to an equivalence respecting the universal bifunctors; no commutativity of the algebras and no further choice beyond the supplied module equivalences and the existence theorem's AC-dependent data is used. [step 3.1, step 3.2, F1, F3, F7] ∎
