entry.title: Graded bimodule maps classify shift-compatible transformations
entry.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $A,B$ graded $k$-algebras and $M,M'$ graded $(B,A)$-bimodules. The map
$$\eta\longmapsto\eta_A,$$
read through the unit isomorphisms $T_M(A)=M\otimes_AA\cong M$ and $T_{M'}(A)\cong M'$, is a
$k$-linear bijection
$$\operatorname{Nat}^{\mathrm{coh}}(T_M,T_{M'})\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\operatorname{Hom}_{B\text{-}A}(M,M')$$
onto the degree-zero $(B,A)$-bimodule maps, with inverse $f\mapsto f\otimes1$. In particular a
coherent transformation between graded tensor functors is determined by its component on the
regular module $A$; that component is automatically degree-zero and right $A$-linear, and conversely
every degree-zero bimodule map induces one and only one coherent transformation. For $A=B=k$
concentrated in degree zero the coherent endomorphisms of the identity functor are the scalars
$k$, and no larger family satisfies the equivariance square.
entry.proof_strategy:
Apply the exact full-faithfulness statement of [[thm-graded-eilenberg-watts-with-coherent-shifts]], with inverse f -> f tensor 1. For the direct check, coherence identifies eta on shifted regular modules, and naturality at r_a gives eta_A(m tensor a)=f(m) tensor a; balancing and the injective tensor unit then give f(ma)=f(m)a. Conversely every degree-zero bimodule map yields a coherent natural transformation by the tensor lemma. The coherent unit T_k -> id transfers endomorphisms to Hom_(k-k)(k,k), whose maps are multiplication by f(1). No choice is used.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: Graded Eilenberg-Watts respects bicategorical coherence
entry.statement:
Let $k$ be a field.

1. The **graded Morita bicategory** $\mathbf{GrBimod}$ has graded $k$-algebras as objects, graded
$(B,A)$-bimodules as 1-cells $A\to B$, degree-zero bimodule maps as 2-cells, composition
$(N,M)\mapsto N\otimes_BM$ on 1-cells and $g\otimes f$ on 2-cells, regular bimodules as identity
1-cells, and the graded associators and unitors of
[[lem-graded-balanced-tensor-and-shift-isomorphisms]] as coherence isomorphisms; it is a bicategory
in the sense of [[def-bicategory-pseudofunctor-and-biequivalence]]: the associators and unitors are
degree-zero natural isomorphisms, they satisfy the pentagon and triangle identities because they are
the ungraded coherence maps of
[[lem-bimodule-tensor-associators-and-unitors-satisfy-bicategory-coherence]] read on graded modules,
and horizontal composition is the functorial tensor product of bimodule maps with
$(g'\otimes f')(g\otimes f)=(g'g)\otimes(f'f)$
([[prop-functoriality-of-module-tensor-products]]).

2. The assignment $\Phi$ of [[thm-graded-eilenberg-watts-with-coherent-shifts]] is a pseudofunctor
from $\mathbf{GrBimod}$ to the bicategory whose objects are the graded $k$-algebras, whose
hom-categories are the $\mathrm{CohFun}(A,B)$ of
[[lem-coherent-shift-functors-and-transformations-form-hom-categories]], whose composition is
composition of coherent functors with the composite comparison, and whose identity 1-cells are the
identity functors with their canonical coherence: the composition comparison
$$T_{N\otimes_BM}\cong T_N\circ T_M$$
is the graded associator of [[lem-graded-balanced-tensor-and-shift-isomorphisms]], the identity
comparison $\mathrm{id}\Rightarrow T_A$ is the inverse graded unitor, and the pseudofunctor coherence equations are
transported from (1).

3. $\Phi$ is a biequivalence: each local functor is an equivalence of categories by
[[cor-graded-bimodule-maps-classify-shift-compatible-transformations]], and it is essentially
surjective on 1-cells because every coherent functor is coherently isomorphic to $T_{F(A)}$ by
[[thm-graded-eilenberg-watts-with-coherent-shifts]]. Horizontal composition of coherent
transformations corresponds to tensoring the underlying graded bimodule maps,
$(g\otimes1)*(f\otimes1)=(g\otimes f)\otimes1$ up to the canonical comparison, so the equivariance
restriction on 2-cells of
[[def-coherently-shift-compatible-functor-and-natural-transformation]] is preserved by the
bicategorical structure. No commutativity beyond $k$, no choice and no enhancement data are
introduced.
entry.proof_strategy:
The graded associators/unitors are the ordinary balanced maps with preserved total internal degree, so [[lem-bimodule-tensor-associators-and-unitors-satisfy-bicategory-coherence]] supplies the pentagon and triangle on the actual bimodule types; tensor-map functoriality supplies composition on 2-cells. The pseudofunctor composition datum is inverse associator T_N T_M -> T_(N tensor_B M); the identity datum is id -> T_A, x -> 1_A tensor x. These coherent comparisons obey the equations of [[def-bicategory-pseudofunctor-and-biequivalence]] by the tensor identities at a variable X. The graded theorem gives local equivalence; Phi is identity on objects, hence a biequivalence. Horizontal composition sends n tensor (m tensor x) to g(n) tensor (f(m) tensor x), corresponding to (g tensor f) tensor 1. No choice or enhancement is used.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: Derived tensor composition and the enhancement boundary
entry.statement:
Let $k$ be a commutative ring and $A,B,C$ graded $k$-algebras. For bounded cochain
complexes $F$ of graded $(B,A)$-bimodules and $G$ of graded $(A,C)$-bimodules
satisfying the projectivity and boundedness hypotheses of the bounded-complex page,
composition of the derived tensor functors corresponds to the degreewise balanced
tensor product with the signed cochain totalization of
[[def-bounded-complex-of-graded-bimodules-and-signed-tensor-totalization]]. Internal
degrees enter only the grading of the total complex, so no additional internal-degree
sign is introduced, and the cochain sign depends only on the cochain degree: this is
the convention of the internal shift $M\{r\}_d=M_{d-r}$ of
[[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]], under which a shifted complex
has the same differential and the same elements, unlike the cochain shift $[1]$ which
has $X[1]^n=X^{n+1}$ and differential $-d_X^{n+1}$, so it lowers cochain
placement by one.

The associativity, unit and cone-compatibility statements and the derived-tensor
equivalences supplied by inverse complexes are exactly those of
[[thm-bounded-bimodule-tensor-associativity-unit-and-cone-compatibility]] and
[[thm-inverse-bimodule-complexes-give-derived-tensor-equivalences]], applied with the
graded balanced associators and unitors of
[[lem-graded-balanced-tensor-and-shift-isomorphisms]]; their projectivity,
boundedness, homotopy and graded/cochain hypotheses are preserved verbatim, with each
coherence identity an identity of underlying graded bimodules checked on elementary
tensors.

This remark asserts **only** that supplied inverse complexes give those equivalences.
It makes no assertion that an arbitrary abstract triangulated functor or natural
transformation between derived categories is induced by a bimodule complex: a dg or
stable enhancement with an appropriate notion of morphism would be needed for such a
classification, and it lies outside this A/B pair. Likewise relative tensor
categories, Radford's $S^4$ theorem, arbitrary Grothendieck categories and schemes are
not prerequisites of this pair, and the internal shift $\{r\}$ of the graded theorem is
the graded-module shift of
[[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]], not the cochain shift $[1]$ of
the bounded-complex page. No commutativity beyond $k$ and no choice are used.

references.title: M. Khovanov and P. Seidel, Quivers, Floer Cohomology, and Braid Group Actions (arXiv:math/0006056), §2a-2c, author pp.8-11 (internal shift {k} and cochain shift [k] with ∂_{M[k]}=(-1)^k∂_M)

entry.title: The degree-zero projection is exact and cocontinuous but not a graded tensor functor
entry.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. An additive $k$-linear functor
$F:\operatorname{GrMod}_0(k)\to\operatorname{GrMod}_0(k)$ that is exact and preserves all
coproducts and satisfies $F(k)=k$ need not be a graded tensor functor: it need not be isomorphic to
$k\otimes_k-$, and it need not admit coherent shift-comparison data at all. So right exactness,
coproduct preservation and even the value on the regular module do not by themselves put a graded
functor into the class classified by
[[thm-graded-eilenberg-watts-with-coherent-shifts]]; the shift-coherence hypothesis of
[[def-coherently-shift-compatible-functor-and-natural-transformation]] is load-bearing.

Let $k$ be a field and let $A=B=k$ be the graded $k$-algebra concentrated in degree $0$
($k_0=k$ and $k_d=0$ for $d\ne0$). Define
$$F:\operatorname{GrMod}_0(k)\longrightarrow\operatorname{GrMod}_0(k),\qquad F(X):=X_0,$$
where $X_0$ is placed in degree $0$ (so $F(X)_0=X_0$ and $F(X)_d=0$ for $d\ne0$), with the evident
$k$-action. Then:

1. $F$ is $k$-linear, exact (left and right exact) and preserves every coproduct, so it satisfies
every hypothesis of the graded Eilenberg-Watts class except shift coherence;
2. $F(k)=k$, so its value at the regular module coincides with that of the tensor functor
$T_k=k\otimes_k-$, which is the identity functor up to the unit isomorphism;
3. nevertheless $F$ is not isomorphic as a functor — hence not coherently isomorphic — to $T_k$: on
the internal shift $k\{1\}$ one has $F(k\{1\})=(k\{1\})_0=k_{-1}=0$, whereas
$T_k(k\{1\})=k\otimes_kk\{1\}\cong k\{1\}\ne0$;
4. consequently $F$ admits no coherent shift-comparison data at all: coherence would require a
degree-zero isomorphism $F(k\{1\})\to F(k)\{1\}=k\{1\}$, impossible because
$F(k\{1\})=0$.

Hence the shift-coherence hypothesis in
[[def-coherently-shift-compatible-functor-and-natural-transformation]] and
[[thm-graded-eilenberg-watts-with-coherent-shifts]] is load-bearing: right exactness, coproduct
preservation and even the value $F(k)=k$ do not classify graded functors by graded bimodules. The
witness is defined without choice. Hazrat's Example 2.3.9 distinguishes equivalences of graded module categories from
shift-commuting equivalences; his Remark 2.3.4 instead concerns natural transformations.
The present witness directly proves failure of shift compatibility without asserting that a
graded tensor functor can fail it.
entry.proof_strategy:
Restrict degree-zero maps to X_0 and place the resulting vector space in degree zero. This operation is k-linear and preserves degreewise kernels, cokernels and arbitrary sums, hence is exact and cocontinuous. At k it gives k; at k{1} it gives zero. Every possible tensor kernel M would satisfy M isomorphic to k by evaluation at k, but its value at k{1} would be M{1}, nonzero. Coherence would separately require theta_(k,1):0 -> k{1}, also impossible. The field condition ensures nonzero k. There is no graded isomorphism k{1} -> k. No choice is used.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: Unrestricted graded natural transformations are not determined by the regular module
entry.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $A=B=k$ the graded $k$-algebra concentrated in degree $0$. The following
over-generalisation is **false**:

> **Refuted claim.** Every natural transformation between graded tensor functors on
> $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(k)$ is determined by its component on the regular module, so that the
> map $\eta\mapsto\eta_A$ is injective on the full hom-collection of natural transformations
> $T_M\Rightarrow T_{M'}$.

It is not so: on the identity functor there are natural transformations with the same component at
$k$ and different components elsewhere, and only the constant scalar families satisfy the
equivariance square of
[[def-coherently-shift-compatible-functor-and-natural-transformation]]. The equivariance
restriction is therefore not vacuous, and dropping it would make the classification of
[[cor-graded-bimodule-maps-classify-shift-compatible-transformations]] false.
entry.proof_strategy:
For any scalar family lambda_d, extend multiplication by lambda_d across finite homogeneous sums. Degree-zero maps preserve degrees, proving naturality. The canonical equivariance square requires lambda_e x=lambda_(e-r) x on X_(e-r); testing X=k{e-r} forces constancy, and constant families satisfy the square. Specify lambda_1=1 and lambda_d=0 for every d!=1: its regular-module component is zero and its k{1} component is nonzero identity. Transport through the tensor unit T_k -> id to obtain two transformations of tensor functors with the same regular component. No choice is used.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: The internal shift as a graded Eilenberg-Watts kernel
entry.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a graded $k$-algebra with $1_A\ne0$. For each $r\in\mathbb Z$ the internal shift functor
$$\{r\}:\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)\longrightarrow\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A),\qquad X\longmapsto X\{r\},$$
is $k$-linear, right exact, coproduct preserving and coherently shift-compatible, and it is
naturally isomorphic to the graded Eilenberg-Watts tensor functor
$$T_{A\{r\}}=A\{r\}\otimes_A-$$
of [[thm-graded-eilenberg-watts-with-coherent-shifts]]: the canonical isomorphisms
$A\{r\}\otimes_AX\cong X\{r\}$ of
[[lem-graded-balanced-tensor-and-shift-isomorphisms]] are natural degree-zero and compatible with
outer actions, so the kernel attached to the internal shift by the theorem is the shifted regular
bimodule $A\{r\}$, and the standard comparisons $\theta^{A\{r\}}$ of
[[lem-graded-tensor-functor-is-k-linear-right-exact-coproduct-preserving-and-shift-coherent]] are
the canonical shift comparisons of
[[lem-internal-shift-endofunctors-and-tensor-compatibility]]. The shift $\{r\}$ is the identity
functor precisely when $r=0$; the hypothesis $1_A\ne0$ is used only for this criterion, since over
the zero algebra the only graded left module is $0$, the module category degenerates and every
shift is the identity there. It is not the cochain (homological) shift $[1]$ of the bounded-complex
page: $X[1]^n=X^{n+1}$, so $[1]$ lowers cochain placement by one and negates the differential, while $\{r\}$ raises
internal degrees and introduces no sign and no differential; the published counterexample
[[cex-internal-and-homological-shifts-are-not-interchangeable]] shows specifically that $\{1\}$ and $[1]$ are not naturally isomorphic on
$K^b(\operatorname{proj}^{gr}A_m)$ for the Khovanov–Seidel algebra $A_m$, $m\ge1$, so the internal and homological
shifts must not be conflated. The example makes no choice.
entry.proof_strategy: Compose the tensor shift isomorphism with the regular tensor unit to obtain A{r} tensor_A X isomorphic to X{r}, coherently and naturally. Evaluate at A to recover the regular shifted kernel. For literal equality with the identity functor, use 1_A!=0 and the disjoint homogeneous pieces to force r=0; the zero algebra is excluded precisely from this criterion. Distinguish cochain shift X[1]^n=X^(n+1), with negated differential and placement lowered by one, from internal regrading with no sign. The cited non-isomorphism example is specifically on K^b(proj^gr A_m), m>=1. No choice is used.

entry.title: Superfluous subobjects and projective covers in an abelian category
entry.statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category and let $n:N\to P$ be a monomorphism, regarded as the subobject $[n]$ of $P$ ([[def-subobject-and-quotient-object]]). The subobject $[n]$ is **superfluous** when for every subobject $[m]:M\to P$ whose join with $[n]$ satisfies $[n]+[m]=[1_P]$ one already has $[m]=[1_P]$ ([[def-the-join-of-subobjects-in-an-abelian-category]]). An epimorphism $\pi:Q\to X$ is **essential** when $\ker\pi$ is a superfluous subobject of $Q$ ([[def-kernels-and-cokernels-as-equalizers-and-coequalizers]], [[def-monomorphism-and-epimorphism]]), and a **projective cover** of $X$ is an essential epimorphism $\pi:Q\to X$ with $Q$ projective ([[def-projective-object]]). On a module category this is exactly the published notion of [[def-essential-epimorphism-and-projective-cover]]: joins of submodules are their sums, so the condition '$N+M=P$ implies $M=P$' is that definition's superfluous-kernel condition verbatim, with the same projective-source requirement. This is the general form of the projective-cover clause of [[def-finite-k-linear-abelian-category]]. The definition asserts no existence, selects no object and uses no choice.
entry.proof_strategy:
This is a definition; the only obligation is the agreement claim with the module notion, and it is definitional: in a module category the join of two submodules is their sum, so 'the only submodule $M\le P$ with $N+M=P$ is $P$' is precisely the superfluous-kernel condition of [[def-essential-epimorphism-and-projective-cover]], and the projective-source clause is identical. No cover existence is assumed here; every later existence hypothesis is stated explicitly.

**Proof technique:** define.

entry.title: Finite-support families of finite-dimensional vector spaces are locally finite but not finite
entry.statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal C$ be the category whose objects are the families $(V_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces with $V_n=0$ for all but finitely many $n$, and whose morphisms $(V_n)\to(W_n)$ are the families $(f_n:V_n\to W_n)$ of $k$-linear maps, with componentwise identities and composition. Then $\mathcal C$ is a $k$-linear abelian category in which kernels, cokernels and finite biproducts are computed componentwise; every hom-space is finite-dimensional over $k$; every object has finite length; every object is projective, hence every simple object has a projective cover; and the objects $S_m$ with $(S_m)_m=k$ and $(S_m)_n=0$ for $n\ne m$ are pairwise non-isomorphic simple objects. Consequently $\mathcal C$ is locally finite and has enough projectives, but it has infinitely many isomorphism classes of simple objects and no object of $\mathcal C$ is a generator, so $\mathcal C$ is not a finite $k$-linear abelian category. No choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
Identify $\mathcal C$ with the full subcategory of the product category $\prod_{n\in\mathbb N}\mathbf{Vect}_k^{\mathrm{fd}}$ ([[def-product-category]]) on the objects of finite support. Each factor is abelian: the category $\mathbf{Vect}_k$ of $k$-vector spaces is the module category $k	ext{-}\mathbf{Mod}$ ([[thm-modules-over-a-ring-form-an-abelian-category]]), and its full subcategory of finite-dimensional spaces is closed under finite direct sums and under kernels and cokernels of its morphisms ([[def-module-homomorphism-kernel-image-and-cokernel]], [[thm-rank-nullity]], [[thm-dimension-formula]], [[def-linear-map]]), so it inherits AB1 and AB2 and is abelian ([[def-abelian-category]], [[def-image-and-coimage-in-a-category-with-kernels-and-cokernels]]); hence the small product is abelian ([[thm-a-small-product-of-abelian-categories-is-abelian]]) with componentwise zero object, biproducts, kernels and cokernels. The finite-support objects contain the zero object, are closed under finite biproducts, and are closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between them (a subobject of a finite-support family has finite support, and the componentwise cokernel of such a map has finite support); these componentwise (co)limits satisfy AB1 and AB2 because they do in every factor, so $\mathcal C$ is abelian. $k$-linearity: $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,W)=\prod_{n\in\operatorname{supp}V\cup\operatorname{supp}W}\operatorname{Hom}_k(V_n,W_n)$ is a finite product of finite-dimensional spaces, hence finite-dimensional ([[def-dimension]], [[def-k-linear-category-and-k-linear-functor]]), and composition is componentwise bilinear. Simples: a nonzero subobject of $S_m$ has a nonzero component in degree $m$, hence is all of $S_m$ ([[def-simple-object]]); conversely a nonzero $V$ has some $V_n
e0$, and a line $L\subseteq V_n$ gives a nonzero subobject isomorphic to $S_n$, so a simple $V$ is isomorphic to some $S_n$; distinct $m$ give non-isomorphic $S_m$ because $(S_m)_n=k$ exactly when $n=m$. Projectivity: $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,-)\cong\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}_k(V_n,(-)_n)$ is a finite product of exact functors, each $V_n$ being a finite direct sum of copies of $k$, which is projective by [[prop-modules-over-a-field-are-projective-flat-and-injective]]; by condition 2 of [[thm-projective-object-characterisations]] every object is projective, and the identity of a simple object is a projective cover since its kernel is zero, which is superfluous ([[def-superfluous-subobject-and-projective-cover-in-an-abelian-category]]). Finite length: induct on $d=\sum_n\dim_kV_n$ ([[def-object-of-finite-length]]); if $d>0$ pick a line $L\subseteq V_n$ in a nonzero degree and form the short exact sequence $0	o S_n	o V	o V/S_n	o0$ ([[def-the-quotient-of-an-object-by-a-subobject]]); the quotient has $\sum\dim=d-1$, so [[thm-length-is-additive-along-a-subobject]] and the induction give $\ell(V)=1+\ell(V/S_n)<\infty$. No generator: if an object $P$ has finite support $F$ and $m
otin F$, then $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(P,S_m)=0=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(0,S_m)$ while $1_{S_m}
e0$, so $\{P\}$ is not separating and $P$ is not a generator ([[def-generator-and-cogenerator-of-a-category]]). All constructions are componentwise and no choice is used.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: Finite-dimensional module categories satisfy the intrinsic finiteness conditions
entry.statement: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional unital algebra over a field $k$, and let $A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ denote the category of finite-dimensional left $A$-modules with $A$-linear maps. Then $A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ is a finite $k$-linear abelian category in the intrinsic sense of [[def-finite-k-linear-abelian-category]]: it is a locally finite $k$-linear abelian category ([[def-locally-finite-k-linear-abelian-category]]); every simple object has a projective cover, namely the cover supplied by [[thm-projective-covers-exist-and-are-unique-for-finite-dimensional-algebras]] and identified with the general notion by [[def-superfluous-subobject-and-projective-cover-in-an-abelian-category]]; and there are finitely many isomorphism classes of simple objects. Moreover every simple left $A$-module is isomorphic to a composition factor of the regular module ${}_AA$, and every finite-dimensional module has length at most its $k$-dimension. No choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
$A	ext{-}\mathrm{mod}$ is a full subcategory of the abelian category of all left $A$-modules ([[thm-modules-over-a-ring-form-an-abelian-category]], [[def-module-homomorphism-kernel-image-and-cokernel]]) that is closed under finite direct sums and under kernels and cokernels of its morphisms: kernels and images of $A$-linear maps of finite-dimensional spaces are finite-dimensional, quotients of finite-dimensional modules are finite-dimensional, and finite direct sums of finite-dimensional modules are finite-dimensional. It therefore inherits AB1 and AB2 and is abelian ([[def-abelian-category]]); its hom-spaces are subspaces of the finite-dimensional spaces $\operatorname{Hom}_k(M,N)$, hence finite-dimensional, and composition is $k$-bilinear, so it is $k$-linear ([[def-k-linear-category-and-k-linear-functor]]). Finite length: a proper inclusion $N\subsetneq M$ strictly increases $k$-dimension, so a strictly decreasing chain of submodules of $M$ has at most $\dim_kM+1$ terms; hence $M$ has a composition series and $\ell(M)\le\dim_kM$ ([[def-object-of-finite-length]], [[def-composition-series-and-composition-factors-of-an-object]]). Enough projectives: the published theorem gives each finite-dimensional module, in particular each simple module, a projective cover in the module sense, which is a projective cover in the sense of [[def-superfluous-subobject-and-projective-cover-in-an-abelian-category]] since the two conditions agree there. Finitely many simples: let $S$ be simple and $0
e s\in S$; the map $\varphi:A	o S$, $\varphi(a)=as$, is $A$-linear with $\varphi(1)=s
e0$, so its image is a nonzero submodule of the simple module $S$ and $\varphi$ is surjective. Take a composition series $0=A_0<\cdots<A_m=A$ of the regular module and let $j\ge1$ be minimal with $\varphi(A_j)
e0$; then $\varphi(A_{j-1})=0$, so $\varphi$ factors through the nonzero simple quotient $A_j/A_{j-1}$ ([[thm-quotient-module-universal-property]], [[def-quotient-module]]), which forces $S\cong A_j/A_{j-1}$ ([[def-simple-module]]). Every simple module is thus one of the finitely many composition factors of ${}_AA$, so there are finitely many simple isomorphism classes. All selections are finite (a composition series of the finite-dimensional module $A$ and its finite factor list), so no choice is used.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: Finite module duality is exact with commuting bimodule actions
entry.statement:
Throughout, a bimodule over $k$-algebras means a $k$-vector space with $k$-bilinear commuting actions and agreeing scalar actions: $(c1_B)m=m(c1_A)=cm$ for $c\in k$ in a $(B,A)$-bimodule. This compatibility is an additional requirement beyond the ring-bimodule definition [[def-bimodule]].

Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional unital algebra over a field $k$, and let
$A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ denote the category of finite-dimensional left
$A$-modules with $A$-linear maps. For such a module $X$ put
$X^{*}=\operatorname{Hom}_k(X,k)=\mathcal L(X,k)$ with the right $A$-action
$(\lambda\cdot a)(x)=\lambda(ax)$, equivalently the left
$A^{\mathrm{op}}$-action $a\cdot\lambda:=\lambda\cdot a$; for an $A$-linear
$u:X\to Y$ put $u^{*}(\lambda)=\lambda\circ u$ for $\lambda\in Y^{*}$. Then:

(i) $(-)^{*}$ is a contravariant $k$-linear functor from
$A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ to the category of finite-dimensional left
$A^{\mathrm{op}}$-modules, and the evaluation
$\operatorname{ev}_X:X\to X^{**}$, $\operatorname{ev}_X(x)(\lambda)=\lambda(x)$,
is a natural isomorphism, so $(-)^{*}$ is a contravariant equivalence;

(ii) $(-)^{*}$ is exact, carrying every short exact sequence
$0\to X\xrightarrow{i}Y\xrightarrow{q}Z\to0$ of finite-dimensional left
$A$-modules to the short exact sequence
$0\to Z^{*}\xrightarrow{q^{*}}Y^{*}\xrightarrow{i^{*}}X^{*}\to0$;

(iii) if $B$ is a unital $k$-algebra and $X$ is a finite-dimensional
$(A,B)$-bimodule, then $X^{*}$ is a $(B,A)$-bimodule under the commuting
actions $(b\cdot\lambda)(x)=\lambda(xb)$ and $(\lambda\cdot a)(x)=\lambda(ax)$,
and duality is a contravariant equivalence between the categories of
finite-dimensional $(A,B)$-bimodules and finite-dimensional $(B,A)$-bimodules,
with the $k$-linear maps that are simultaneously $A$-linear and $B$-linear as
morphisms.

No choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
Use k-bilinear commuting actions with agreeing k-scalars. Define dual actions and transpose maps, verify their module laws and natural double-dual evaluation. Extend a finite basis along an injection to prove dual surjectivity; rank-nullity identifies middle kernel and image. Evaluation is linear for both actions, giving the bimodule duality. Only finitely many bases and extensions are chosen.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: Projective epimorphisms onto the simples generate every finite-length object
entry.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a locally finite $k$-linear abelian category with finitely
many isomorphism classes of simple objects, represented by $S_1,\dots,S_n$, and
suppose that for each $i$ a projective epimorphism $Q_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$
is chosen (for instance the projective cover supplied by
[[def-superfluous-subobject-and-projective-cover-in-an-abelian-category]] when
$\mathcal C$ is finite in the intrinsic sense). Then for every object $X$ of
finite length there are integers $m_i\ge0$ and an epimorphism
$\bigoplus_{i=1}^nQ_i^{m_i}\twoheadrightarrow X$; in particular, with
$P=\bigoplus_iQ_i$, every object of $\mathcal C$ admits an epimorphism
$P^m\twoheadrightarrow X$ for some $m\ge0$. Only the finitely many chosen maps
$Q_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ are selected, and no other choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
Induct on length, starting at the zero object. If Y is the penultimate composition-series object, the induction source is W=the finite biproduct of Q_j^{m_j}. Lift a chosen projective epimorphism onto the final simple quotient. A map annihilating W plus this lift factors through the quotient and is zero by epic cancellation, so the combined map is epic. Regroup the finite summands and use the split projection from P^{sum m_i}.

**Proof technique:** induction.

entry.title: Intrinsic finite category hypotheses give a finite projective generator
entry.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a finite $k$-linear abelian category, with simple
representatives $S_1,\dots,S_n$ and chosen projective covers
$Q_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$, and put $P=\bigoplus_{i=1}^nQ_i$ and
$A=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(P)^{\mathrm{op}}$. Then: (i) $P$ is
projective; (ii) $P$ is a generator of $\mathcal C$, that is, $\{P\}$ is
separating; (iii) $A$ is a finite-dimensional unital $k$-algebra; (iv)
$\mathcal C(P,-)$ is exact and faithful; and (v) every object of $\mathcal C$ is
a quotient of a finite direct sum of copies of $P$. The proof uses only that
each $Q_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ is a projective epimorphism, never the
superfluity of its kernel, so the same conclusions hold if "enough projectives"
is read as "every simple object admits a projective epimorphism onto it"; for
the finite module categories of
[[prop-finite-dimensional-module-categories-are-intrinsically-finite]] the two
readings coincide. Only the finitely many covers $Q_i$ are selected; no further
choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
Lift each entire injection Q_i into P along an epimorphism onto P; coproduct uniqueness gives a section, so P is projective. For a nonzero image Z, lift onto a simple quotient from Q_i; the resulting h:Q_i into Z is nonzero, not necessarily epic. Lift again through X onto Z and compose with the split projection P onto Q_i to separate distinct maps. End(P)^op is finite-dimensional with central scalar units; projectivity gives Hom exactness, separation gives faithfulness and the covering lemma gives finite quotients.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: Finite abelian categories admit finite-dimensional module models
entry.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a finite $k$-linear abelian category, let $S_1,\dots,S_n$ be
representatives of its simple objects with chosen projective covers
$Q_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$, and put $P=\bigoplus_iQ_i$ and
$A=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(P)^{\mathrm{op}}$. Then $A$ is a
finite-dimensional unital $k$-algebra and
$H=\mathcal C(P,-):\mathcal C\to A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ is a fully faithful, essentially surjective $k$-linear
functor, where $A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ is the category of
finite-dimensional left $A$-modules: $H$ is faithful, full and exact, and every
finite-dimensional left $A$-module is isomorphic to $H(X)$ for some object $X$
of $\mathcal C$, with the preimage exhibited by the finite-presentation
construction in the proof. If a splitting of essential surjectivity is additionally supplied — an object $X_V$ and an isomorphism $H(X_V)\to V$ for every target module $V$ — then $H$ is a $k$-linear equivalence in the specified-quasi-inverse sense of [[def-equivalence-and-adjoint-equivalence-of-categories]]. Conversely any such $k$-linear equivalence from a finite-dimensional module category transfers the intrinsic finiteness conditions, so the usual equivalence formulation holds when these splitting data are supplied. Fullness, faithfulness, exactness and objectwise essential surjectivity use only finite choices. Selecting finite presentations separately for each $V$ does not itself supply a simultaneous splitting; no choice-free existence of that splitting is asserted.
entry.proof_strategy:
Use H(X)=C(P,X) with A=End(P)^op acting by precomposition. Projectivity and separation give exactness and faithfulness. From the finite presentation P^s -> P^r -> X -> 0, apply H in the same covariant direction, obtaining A^s -> A^r -> H(X) -> 0. Maps from finite free modules come from biproduct components; faithfulness and cokernel factorisation give fullness. A finite presentation of each target module gives an objectwise preimage by a cokernel. A specified quasi-inverse is constructed only from supplied simultaneous preimages and isomorphisms, using unique lifts on morphisms. Conversely an equivalence transfers kernels, cokernels, simple subobjects, projectivity and superfluity.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: Finite Eilenberg–Watts for right exact linear functors
entry.statement:
Throughout, a bimodule over $k$-algebras means a $k$-vector space with $k$-bilinear commuting actions and agreeing scalar actions: $(c1_B)m=m(c1_A)=cm$ for $c\in k$ in a $(B,A)$-bimodule. This compatibility is an additional requirement beyond the ring-bimodule definition [[def-bimodule]].

For assertions forming categories of functors, fix a set of allowed finite-dimensional $k$-vector space structures containing $k$ and the underlying spaces of the algebras considered, and closed under finite biproducts, subspaces, quotients, $k$-tensor products, $k$-duals and spaces of linear maps. Allow every compatible algebra, module and bimodule structure on these spaces. The resulting module categories are small, so their functors and natural transformations are set-coded as required by [[def-functor-category]]. The objectwise formulas apply without this size restriction; no category of proper-class functors is asserted.

Let $A$ and $B$ be finite-dimensional unital algebras over a field $k$, and let
$A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ and $B\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ be the categories of
finite-dimensional left modules.

(i) For every finite-dimensional $(B,A)$-bimodule $M$ the functor
$T_M=M\otimes_A-:A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\to B\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ is well
defined, $k$-linear and right exact.

(ii) Conversely every $k$-linear right exact functor
$F:A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\to B\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ is naturally isomorphic to
$T_{F(A)}$, where $F(A)$ carries the $(B,A)$-bimodule structure of
[[lem-evaluation-on-the-regular-module-has-a-commuting-right-action]];
explicitly the canonical comparison $\tau_X:F(A)\otimes_AX\to F(X)$,
$\tau_X(m\otimes x)=F(\ell_x)(m)$ with $\ell_x(a)=ax$, is a natural
isomorphism.

(iii) For finite-dimensional $(B,A)$-bimodules $M,M'$ the assignment
$f\mapsto(f\otimes1_X)_X$ is a bijection
$\operatorname{Hom}_{B\text{-}A}(M,M')\to\operatorname{Nat}(T_M,T_{M'})$,
compatible with addition, identities and vertical composition.

(iv) Hence $M\mapsto T_M$ is an equivalence of categories between the category
of finite-dimensional $(B,A)$-bimodules with bimodule maps and the category of
$k$-linear right exact functors $A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\to B\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$
with all natural transformations. No commutativity of $A$ or $B$ is assumed and
no choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
Work with agreeing k-scalar actions and the stated small allowed-space setting when forming functor categories. Finite basis tensors span M tensor_A X, so tensor functors stay finite. Evaluation F(A) has ma=F(r_a)(m), and k-linearity gives m(c1_A)=cm. The balanced canonical comparison uses only A, X and ell_x, so the all-module calculations restrict to finite modules. It is the unit at A and an isomorphism on finite biproducts. A finite presentation and cokernel universality extend the isomorphism to X. Naturality at r_a and ell_x classifies all transformations by bimodule maps. Evaluation at A is an explicit quasi-inverse, with comparison natural in F and tensor-unit natural in M; no simultaneous selection is required.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: Finite left exact functors are Hom functors with dual bimodule kernels
entry.statement:
Throughout, a bimodule over $k$-algebras means a $k$-vector space with $k$-bilinear commuting actions and agreeing scalar actions: $(c1_B)m=m(c1_A)=cm$ for $c\in k$ in a $(B,A)$-bimodule. This compatibility is an additional requirement beyond the ring-bimodule definition [[def-bimodule]].

For assertions forming categories of functors, fix a set of allowed finite-dimensional $k$-vector space structures containing $k$ and the underlying spaces of the algebras considered, and closed under finite biproducts, subspaces, quotients, $k$-tensor products, $k$-duals and spaces of linear maps. Allow every compatible algebra, module and bimodule structure on these spaces. The resulting module categories are small, so their functors and natural transformations are set-coded as required by [[def-functor-category]]. The objectwise formulas apply without this size restriction; no category of proper-class functors is asserted.

Let $A,B$ be finite-dimensional unital algebras over a field $k$. Let
${}_AA_A$ be the regular bimodule and let $A^{*}=\operatorname{Hom}_k(A,k)$ be
its $k$-dual with the commuting actions $(a\cdot\lambda)(x)=\lambda(xa)$ and
$(\lambda\cdot a)(x)=\lambda(ax)$, regarded as a left $A$-module. Let
$F:A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\to B\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ be a $k$-linear left exact
functor and put $M=F(A^{*})$ with the right $A$-action
$m\cdot a=F(\lambda\mapsto\lambda\cdot a)(m)$; then $M$ is a
finite-dimensional $(B,A)$-bimodule. There is a natural isomorphism of left
$B$-modules

$$F(X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^{*},X)$$

for every finite-dimensional left $A$-module $X$, where $M^{*}$ is the
$(A,B)$-bimodule dual to $M$ and the left $B$-action on the Hom is
$(b\varphi)(u)=\varphi(u\cdot b)$; the isomorphism is natural in $X$.
Consequently $M\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^{*},-)$ is an equivalence of
categories between finite-dimensional $(B,A)$-bimodules with bimodule maps and
$k$-linear left exact functors $A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\to B\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$
with all natural transformations, with quasi-inverse $F\mapsto F(A^{*})$. No
commutativity of $A$ or $B$ and no choice are used.
entry.proof_strategy:
Use the agreeing-scalar and small allowed-space conventions. A* is an (A,A)-bimodule; its right multiplications are in F domain and induce the right A-action on M=F(A*). Exact finite duality converts left exact F to right exact F^d:A^op-mod -> B^op-mod. Finite Eilenberg-Watts gives K=M* with left A/right B actions. Interpret K as right A^op and X* as left A^op; evaluation u tensor lambda -> lambda(phi(u)) identifies the dual tensor with Hom_A(M*,X), with right B before dualizing and left B after dualizing. Tensor-Hom adjunction proves these Hom functors land in Lex. Yoneda and naturality at right B-multiplications classify transformations by dual bimodule maps. Evaluation at A* is an explicit quasi-inverse; Hom_A(M*,A*) identifies naturally with M by phi -> m with u(m)=phi(u)(1), inverse m -> (u -> (a -> u(ma))).

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: Finite one-sided exactness is equivalent to existence of the corresponding adjoint
entry.statement: Let $A,B$ be finite-dimensional unital algebras over a field $k$ and let $F:A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\to B\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ be a $k$-linear functor between the categories of finite-dimensional left modules. Then: (i) $F$ is right exact if and only if $F$ has a right adjoint; more precisely, if $F$ is right exact then $F\cong T_{F(A)}$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_B(F(A),-)$ is a right adjoint taking finite-dimensional modules to finite-dimensional modules, while a functor with a right adjoint preserves every finite colimit that exists in $A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ and hence is right exact. (ii) $F$ is left exact if and only if $F$ has a left adjoint; if $F$ is left exact then $F\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^{*},-)$ with $M=F(A^{*})$ and $M^{*}\otimes_B-$ is a left adjoint, while a functor with a left adjoint preserves every finite limit that exists and hence is left exact. No commutativity and no choice are used.
entry.proof_strategy:
(i) If $F$ is right exact then $F\cong T_{F(A)}$ by [[thm-finite-eilenberg-watts-for-right-exact-linear-functors]], and $T_{F(A)}$ is left adjoint to $\operatorname{Hom}_B(F(A),-)$ by [[lem-tensor-hom-adjunction-for-bimodules]]; for finite-dimensional $Y$ the space $\operatorname{Hom}_B(F(A),Y)$ is finite-dimensional because $F(A)$ and $Y$ are, so the adjoint stays in the finite module categories ([[def-dimension]]). Conversely if $F$ has a right adjoint $G$, then $F$ is a left adjoint and preserves every colimit that exists ([[cor-left-adjoints-preserve-colimits]]); since $A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ is abelian it has all finite colimits, so $F$ preserves finite colimits and is right exact ([[def-left-exact-and-right-exact-functor]], [[def-module-homomorphism-kernel-image-and-cokernel]]). (ii) If $F$ is left exact then $F\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^{*},-)$ with $M=F(A^{*})$ by [[thm-finite-left-exact-functors-are-hom-functors-with-dual-bimodule-kernels]], and $M^{*}\otimes_B-$ is left adjoint to $\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^{*},-)$ by [[lem-tensor-hom-adjunction-for-bimodules]] applied to the $(A,B)$-bimodule $M^{*}$; the left adjoint preserves the finite module categories because $M^{*}\otimes_BY$ is a quotient of $M^{*}\otimes_kY$ and so finite-dimensional. Conversely if $F$ has a left adjoint then $F$ is a right adjoint and preserves every limit that exists ([[thm-right-adjoints-preserve-limits]]); all finite limits exist in $A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$, so $F$ is left exact ([[def-left-exact-and-right-exact-functor]]). No commutativity and no choice are used.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: Finite Eilenberg–Watts is a biequivalence
entry.statement:
Throughout, a bimodule over $k$-algebras means a $k$-vector space with $k$-bilinear commuting actions and agreeing scalar actions: $(c1_B)m=m(c1_A)=cm$ for $c\in k$ in a $(B,A)$-bimodule. This compatibility is an additional requirement beyond the ring-bimodule definition [[def-bimodule]].

For assertions forming categories of functors, fix a set of allowed finite-dimensional $k$-vector space structures containing $k$ and the underlying spaces of the algebras considered, and closed under finite biproducts, subspaces, quotients, $k$-tensor products, $k$-duals and spaces of linear maps. Allow every compatible algebra, module and bimodule structure on these spaces. The resulting module categories are small, so their functors and natural transformations are set-coded as required by [[def-functor-category]]. The objectwise formulas apply without this size restriction; no category of proper-class functors is asserted.

Let $A,B$ range over finite-dimensional unital algebras over a field $k$, and
consider the assignment $\Phi(A)=A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$,
$\Phi(M)=T_M=M\otimes_A-$, $\Phi(f)=f\otimes1$ on finite-dimensional bimodules
and bimodule maps. (i) For all $A,B$ the assignment $M\mapsto T_M$ is an
equivalence of categories between finite-dimensional $(B,A)$-bimodules with
bimodule maps and $k$-linear right exact functors
$A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\to B\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ with all natural
transformations, so it is full, faithful and essentially surjective. (ii) The
composition and unit comparisons of the pseudofunctor
[[lem-tensoring-defines-a-pseudofunctor-with-interchange]] restrict to
finite-dimensional algebras and finite-dimensional modules: the associativity
isomorphism $N\otimes_B(M\otimes_A-)\cong(N\otimes_BM)\otimes_A-$ with
components $N\otimes_B(M\otimes_AX)\cong(N\otimes_BM)\otimes_AX$ and the inverse unit
isomorphism $X\cong A\otimes_AX$ are natural isomorphisms of
finite-dimensional modules, and the pseudofunctor coherence equations remain
satisfied. Consequently these data define a biequivalence from the bicategory
of finite-dimensional algebras, finite-dimensional bimodules and bimodule maps
to the 2-category of finite-dimensional module categories, $k$-linear right
exact functors and natural transformations. No commutativity and no choice are
used.
entry.proof_strategy:
Use agreeing scalars and the common set of allowed spaces, so every finite module source is small and functor hom-categories consist of set-coded objects and maps. The local tensor assignment is the equivalence with explicit evaluation quasi-inverse supplied by finite Eilenberg-Watts. Tensor products of finite bimodules remain finite. Use composition comparison alpha inverse and unit comparison lambda inverse, X -> A tensor_A X. Check associativity, unit paths and horizontal naturality directly on elementary tensors under those comparisons. Each target object A-mod is Phi(A), so the biequivalence criterion applies. The schematic unrestricted supplier is used only for its explicit comparison formulas.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: Exact finite tensor functors have projective right-module kernels
entry.statement:
Throughout, a bimodule over $k$-algebras means a $k$-vector space with $k$-bilinear commuting actions and agreeing scalar actions: $(c1_B)m=m(c1_A)=cm$ for $c\in k$ in a $(B,A)$-bimodule. This compatibility is an additional requirement beyond the ring-bimodule definition [[def-bimodule]].

Let $A,B$ be finite-dimensional unital algebras over a field $k$ and let $M$ be
a finite-dimensional $(B,A)$-bimodule with associated tensor functor
$T_M=M\otimes_A-:A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\to B\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$. Then the
following are equivalent: (1) $T_M$ is exact on finite-dimensional left
$A$-modules, equivalently $M$ is flat as a right $A$-module; (2) $M$ is a
projective right $A$-module. Since $M$ is finite-dimensional, (2) is also
equivalent to $M$ being a direct summand of a finite free right $A$-module and
to $M$ being finitely generated and projective. No choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
Require agreeing k-scalar actions. Projective M is flat, so its tensor functor is exact on all left modules and thus on finite ones. In the other direction exact finite duality and the balanced functional pairing give (M tensor_A X)* = Hom_{A^op}(M,X*). Exactness of tensor on finite left modules gives exactness of Hom on finite right modules. Lift 1_M through a finite free cover p:A^n onto M to obtain h with ph=1. For an arbitrary surjection e:E onto N prime and f:M into N prime, choose finite basis lifts of fp:A^n into N prime and compose with h. Thus M is projective against arbitrary targets without AC. Finite generation and the finite-free-summand criterion complete all equivalences.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: A finite right exact functor needs no infinite-coproduct hypothesis
entry.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $A=k[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^{2})$ be the algebra of
dual numbers ([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]],
[[def-quotient-ring]]) and let $S=A/(\varepsilon)$ be its simple module
([[def-simple-module]]). Then: (i) $A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ has no countable
coproduct of copies of $A$, so it is not cocomplete; (ii) nevertheless the functor
$T_S=S\otimes_A-$, the case $M=S$ of the finite Eilenberg–Watts theorem, is
right exact with right adjoint $\operatorname{Hom}_A(S,-)$, and it is classified
by its kernel $T_S(A)\cong S$. Its right exactness, its right adjoint and its
classification use only finite free presentations and the finite biproducts of
$A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$; no infinite coproducts are formed. Thus the finite classification requires no additional preservation hypothesis about infinite coproducts. Preservation of coproducts that do exist remains a meaningful condition; nonexistence of one countable coproduct does not make that condition vacuous. No choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
For the nonzero simple quotient S, Hom_A(A,S)=S by evaluation at 1. If a countable coproduct of regular modules existed in the finite category, restriction along its injections would give a k-linear bijection Hom_A(X,S) -> S^N. Explicit finite-support e_n are independent, contradicting finite dimension of Hom_A(X,S). Yet T_S is right exact, has the finite Hom right adjoint and kernel S by the finite classification and tensor unit. No infinite coproduct assumption is used. The all-module theorem has a distinct unrestricted domain; preservation of existing coproducts is meaningful, and a countable family of zeros has coproduct zero. No semisimplicity refutation is needed.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: Finite length and finite Hom do not imply a finite category
entry.statement: The statement 'a $k$-linear abelian category with finite-dimensional hom-spaces, finite-length objects and enough projective covers is finite' is false. The category $\mathcal C$ of finite-support $\mathbb N$-indexed families of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces with componentwise maps is $k$-linear and abelian, has finite-dimensional hom-spaces, every object has finite length and every simple object has a projective cover, but the objects $S_m$ concentrated in a single degree are pairwise non-isomorphic simple objects, so $\mathcal C$ has infinitely many isomorphism classes of simple objects; moreover no object of $\mathcal C$ is a generator. Hence local finiteness together with enough projectives does not imply the fourth intrinsic finiteness condition of [[def-finite-k-linear-abelian-category]]. No choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
All the asserted properties of $\mathcal C$ are proved in [[lem-finite-support-families-of-finite-dimensional-vector-spaces-are-locally-finite]]: $\mathcal C$ is $k$-linear and abelian with componentwise (co)limits, hom-spaces are finite-dimensional, every object has finite length, every object is projective (so every simple object has a projective cover, [[def-superfluous-subobject-and-projective-cover-in-an-abelian-category]]), the $S_m$ are pairwise non-isomorphic simple objects, and no object is a generator ([[def-generator-and-cogenerator-of-a-category]]). Since the intrinsic definition of a finite $k$-linear abelian category requires finitely many simple isomorphism classes, $\mathcal C$ is locally finite with enough projectives but not finite; this is exactly the failure of clause (iv) while clauses (i)-(iii) hold. No choice is used.

**Proof technique:** direct.

entry.title: The dual-numbers tensor functor is right exact but not left exact
entry.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $A=k[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^{2})$ be the algebra of
dual numbers ([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]],
[[def-quotient-ring]]) and let $S=A/(\varepsilon)$ be its simple module
([[def-simple-module]]). Then the tensor functor
$T_S=S\otimes_A-:A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}\to A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ is right exact
but not left exact. Explicitly, applied to the non-split short exact sequence
$0\to(\varepsilon)\to A\to S\to0$ of finite-dimensional $A$-modules it yields,
under the identifications $S\otimes_A(\varepsilon)\cong S$, $S\otimes_AA\cong S$
and $S\otimes_AS\cong S$, the sequence
$S\xrightarrow{0}S\xrightarrow{\cong}S\to0$; the comparison map
$S\otimes_A(\varepsilon)\to S\otimes_AA$ is zero and therefore is not
injective, so $T_S$ is not left exact. Consistently, $T_S$ has a right adjoint
$\operatorname{Hom}_A(S,-)$ but no left adjoint, and its kernel $S$ is not a
projective right $A$-module. No choice is used.
entry.proof_strategy:
A has basis 1,epsilon with epsilon squared zero; S=A/(epsilon) is one-dimensional, simple, and isomorphic to the ideal (epsilon). The sequence 0 -> (epsilon) -> A -> S -> 0 cannot split, because epsilon acts nontrivially on A and trivially on S plus S. Right exact tensoring gives the sequence S -> S -> S -> 0; its first map is zero and its second map is an isomorphism. Thus this sequence is exact at the middle term; failure of left exactness is failure of injectivity of the first map from nonzero S. The adjoint corollary gives a right adjoint and no left adjoint; projective kernels would give exactness, so S is not right projective. No published semisimplicity refutation is needed.

**Proof technique:** direct.
